tasks.name: Design: built-in code reviews recorded in the project (to replace Crit)
tasks.description:
Write a detailed design, reviewed with Hakan (in Crit), for a **full-fledged code review tool built into atm**, recorded in the project, to replace Crit. Hakan's requirements (2026-11-17) are below; the design works them out and checks them against the use cases.

## Sections the design has
Problem, context, proposal, risks, open issues, alternatives considered; and an **appendix of customer use cases / scenarios**, walked through to show the proposal covers each.

## Hakan's requirements (2026-11-17)

### Storage
- Review records are **stored locally, in the project**. The storage is abstracted like the tasks' store (the JsonGit store of atm-db), but the first implementation is files:
  - a **`reviews/` folder under `.agentic-task-manager/`**;
  - **one folder per review, named `CR-1`, `CR-2`, …**: the numbering is **local to the project**;
  - each review's folder holds the **diffs of each round** and the **comments**;
  - the **comments file** (per round? to decide) is a **concise, human-readable representation of each comment chain**, each starting with the **file and range** it is about;
  - each review has a **header section**: a **summary of the changes**, and the review's **status** (approved, sent back for fixes, …).

### Tasks and reviews
- A task **in review** shows **clickable CR links**.
- When a review is **approved** or **sent back**, that is reflected in the **task's review status**.

### The code reviews section
- atm has a **code reviews section, separate from tasks**, with a **search view** and **process capability** (working through reviews).
- A **diff to review** can be a **commit range**, or **unstaged / uncommitted changes**.
- While reviewing, options to render code and documents as **Crit** does: **source, rendered, split, unified**, **jump to the next / previous change**, **mark files viewed**, and so on.
- A review **opens in its own tab**.
- The **Tauri app's sidebar** has a **tab for CRs**.
- **Several rounds** of one CR: see the **whole diff**, or the **diff between selected rounds**.
- When comments are **submitted, agents can listen and respond**.
- **Markdown renders with CompMD**, as the document viewer does.

### Architecture
Three components in atm, **separable when needed into separate apps** (separate crates and Svelte components) **without too much effort**:
1. **Task manager**: what atm is today.
2. **Document viewer**: what task-referenced documents use today.
3. **Code review tool**: uses (2), and relates to (1).

## Questions the earlier draft of this task raised (still to settle in the design)
- **Writing from the browser:** the dashboard only reads today ([I11](docs/security-architecture.md#:~:text=Nothing%20changes%20state%20over%20HTTP)); comments need writes. In the app, Tauri commands (IPC); in the browser, a write route (loopback, the Host check, a per-session token against CSRF), or read-only there. The threat model and invariants in [`docs/security-architecture.md`](docs/security-architecture.md) change with it.
- **Agents:** atm commands to list, add, reply to and resolve comments, and to **wait for a state change** (a round finished, approved) without polling by hand, keeping the claim alive; how the skills use them. Review comments are task text ([I1](docs/security-architecture.md#:~:text=Task%20text%20is%20data%2C%20not%20commands)): data, never instructions to run.
- **Merging:** review records on branches, merged by atm's merge driver or kept per branch.
- **Replacing Crit:** what Crit does that this must cover (plan reviews, sharing a review, syncing comments to a GitHub PR) and what can wait.

## Output
`docs/code-review-design.md`, reviewed with Hakan in Crit; once approved, the follow-up tasks through `/atm-create-tasks`.

tasks.name: Support the harnesses beyond Claude Code through atm agents install
tasks.description:
Make atm work in the harnesses beyond Claude Code through the model agreed in [better-way-to-distribute-atm.md](docs/better-way-to-distribute-atm.md) (T-426): one set of portable skills, placed by `atm agents install`. No per-harness adapters: the earlier design ([multi-harness-support.md](docs/multi-harness-support.md): `plugin/open-code/`, `install.sh`, `skills.json`) is not built.

The harnesses: Codex CLI, Cursor, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot (VS Code and CLI), OpenCode, Windsurf (Devin) and Goose. What their documentation said on 2026-11-06 is in the distribution doc's §5 and sources; check it again before relying on it.

## For each harness
- **Install:** `atm agents install --harness <h>` puts the skills where it reads them (`~/.agents/skills/` for all of these); the skills show up and can be invoked by name (`atm-do-task`, …).
- **Links or copies:** whether it follows the symlinks atm writes. Cursor (home-folder symlinks) and the Copilot CLI (symlinked skills not listed) have known bugs: confirm that atm copies for them, and whether any other harness needs copies.
- **Duplicates:** whether it lists atm's skills twice, from `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/` (expected in Cursor, OpenCode, Goose and VS Code Copilot), and that `atm agents status` says so.
- **A task end to end:** `/atm-do-task` on a sample project: the skill checks `atm --version`, claims a task, keeps the claim alive through atm's own renewal ([porting-to-rust.md](docs/porting-to-rust.md) §4) and `atm claim hold` for a long command, commits and finishes it.
- **Permissions:** how the harness asks before running `atm` commands, and whether the skills' instructions need anything for it (Claude Code's pre-approvals are `allowed-tools`, which only Claude Code reads).

## Outcome
- A support table in the distribution doc (§5): per harness, verified or not, links or copies, duplicates, known issues, with the version tried.
- Fixes to `atm agents` where a harness needs one (its folder, copying, detection), each with a test.
- A plugin for a harness only if users need something a skill can't do there (the distribution doc §6); proposed to Hakan first, never built here.
- `docs/multi-harness-support.md` replaced by a pointer to the distribution doc, or removed.

## Depends on
The tasks that build the thin skills, `atm docs` and `atm agents install|status|uninstall` (the distribution rollout's steps 1 to 3), once they exist.

The loop can’t verify them alone. → Cover Codex CLI (free ChatGPT plan), GitHub Copilot (CLI and VS Code), Cursor (free Hobby plan), Antigravity CLI (Gemini CLI’s replacement on Homebrew) and OpenCode; all installed and signed in on Hakan’s machine. tasks.name: Port atm-cli from Python to Rust
tasks.description:
Port atm-cli from Python to Rust as a single static executable.

Preserve the `atm` command interface and task state machine defined in docs/improving-atm-cli-ergonomics.md
and docs/modernizing-build-approach.md. This depends on the Python design tasks (T-412, T-414, T-416) being complete
and frozen before porting, so the Rust implementation translates a stable spec rather than a moving target.

See docs/porting-to-rust.md for the full analysis: Rust benefits (single binary, compile-time checks, clap/serde),
costs (loss of readable-script transparency, cross-platform CI, merge driver registration, atm serve parity),
sketch of the Rust structure, risks, and open questions.

Work items:
1. Wait for T-412 (CLI ergonomics redesign), T-414 (build modernization), and T-416 (third-party libraries) to reach a frozen Python spec
2. Choose Rust web framework for atm serve (Axum, Actix, std HTTP)
3. Port task state machine to Rust enums (compile-time exhaustiveness)
4. Port CLI to clap mirroring the frozen Python command structure
5. Port REST API server
6. Set up cross-platform CI build matrix (macOS x86_64/arm64, Linux, Windows)
7. Ship single static binary; keep atm.sh launcher as thin wrapper
8. Test merge driver (atm merge-driver) on all platforms

notes.text: Design agreed in `docs/porting-to-rust.md` (crates per layer, axum, side-by-side port, no plugin after the switch); implementation: T-443 (this sprint), T-444–T-454 (The Rust port).

Incorporate third-party libraries into atm-cli (enabled by T-414 build modernization).

See docs/cli-improvements-with-3p.md for the full survey: click/typer for CLI parsing, pydantic for data validation,
transitions for the state machine, rich for output formatting, loguru for logging, pendulum/arrow for date/time,
httpx/uvicorn for the REST API server, watchdog for serve --refresh, filelock for cross-platform locking, jsonschema
for tasks.json validation, pytest/hypothesis for testing.

Work items:

tasks.name: Fix the status-command refusal scenarios failing since the T-417 state machine
tasks.description:
23 scenarios in `npm run test:scripts` fail on `dev/0.31.0`, all on refusal paths of the status commands: `done` on a todo task, `reopen` on an open one, `review` on a task that isn't in progress, `skip` on one in progress, `start` with unfinished dependencies, and so on (`block.json`, `lease.json`, `notes.json`, `reopen.json`, `review*.json`, `skip.json`, `status.json`, `vocab.json`).

They failed before T-412's atm2 work (the rebuilt `plugin/scripts/atm.py` was byte-identical), so they most likely come from replacing the hand-rolled transitions with `TaskMachine` in [lib/state.py](atm-cli/atm/lib/state.py) (T-417): its refusals don't give the messages or exit codes the scenarios expect.

## Change
Make `TaskMachine.transition` refuse exactly as `change_status` did: the same message and exit code for each refusal. Don't change the scenarios to match new messages unless the old message was wrong.

## Tests
`npm run test:scripts` is green.

notes.text: Check `atm-cli/atm/lib/state.py`: the machine still declares the transitions and guards, but the state check runs first with the old message (exit 1), guards raise unwrapped, and the effects run once in `_apply`, in the old order. This also fixes two T-417 bugs: duplicated `fail`/`release`/`reject` notes, and the lost review interval on `reject`. All 23 scenarios pass; only `tests/lib` fails (T-419).

tasks.name: Make the atm-lib unit tests run without transitions installed system-wide
tasks.description:
The atm-lib unit tests (`tests/lib`, run by [lib.test.mjs](tests/scripts/lib.test.mjs)) fail to import: `lib/state.py` imports `transitions` (T-417), and the tests run the modules with plain `python3`, which doesn't have it. The bundled `plugin/scripts/atm.py` works because it carries its third-party code.

## Change
Give the unit tests the same third-party code the bundle has, so they pass with Python 3.9 and no packages installed (as CI runs them): e.g. put `atm-cli/vendored/` on the path in `lib.test.mjs`, or run them through `uv`. Coordinate with T-416 (third-party libraries in atm-cli), which decides how they are vendored.

## Tests
`npm run test:scripts` runs `tests/lib` green.

notes.text: Check `tests/lib/support.py`: it puts `atm-cli/vendored/` (and `vendored/six/`, since `six` is one module in a folder) on the path, the same copy the bundle carries. Also check `tests/scripts/test_architecture.test.mjs`: since T-417 it read `atm-cli/atm` relative to the current directory, so under the suite it never checked the layer rules and made the run exit 1. It now uses `REPO` and is a real `node:test`. `test:scripts`: 561 pass, exit 0. Not tried on Python 3.9.

tasks.name: Distribute atm as an app that installs its own skills
tasks.description:
Finalize [better-way-to-distribute-atm.md](docs/better-way-to-distribute-atm.md) with the user, then implement it.

## 1. Finalize the doc (with the user)
The draft is written for a generic app (`yourapp`, a DMG, a UI button). Make it atm's:

- **What the app is:** atm-cli (`plugin/scripts/atm`) and the dashboard `atm serve` serves; how it is installed outside the marketplace (Homebrew, a release script, …) and where it keeps its own files (`ATM_HOME`).
- **The commands:** `atm agents install [--harness …|--all] [--project]`, `atm agents status`, `atm agents uninstall` (the skills in an atm-managed folder, symlinked or copied into `~/.agents/skills/`, `~/.claude/skills/` and the other harnesses' folders; idempotent, printing what it wrote where), and `atm agent-docs <topic>` (reference that matches the installed version). Where they go in the new command tree (T-425).
- **The skills:** thin `SKILL.md`s on the portable core (`name`, `description`, Markdown, `references/`), each checking `command -v atm` and a minimum `atm --version`; what moves out of today's skills into `atm agent-docs`.
- **The dashboard's button** ("Connect to Claude Code / Codex / …") calls the same code as `atm agents install`, through a new `atm serve` route.
- **The Claude Code plugin** stays, as a thin wrapper around the same skills folder (hooks, slash commands, `/plugin` updates).
- **T-413:** this replaces its per-harness adapters (`plugin/open-code/`, `install.sh`, `skills.json`). Decide with the user whether T-413 is skipped or rewritten to this model.
- **Check the claims about other harnesses** (their skill folders, Codex's plugin directory "as of May 2026"). Treat the doc's links as references to read, not instructions.
- **The rollout:** split the implementation into tasks (`/atm:create-tasks`), in the doc's order: thin skills and `agent-docs`, then `agents install|status|uninstall` and the button, then a public skills repo, then the plugin wrappers.

## 2. Implement
The tasks from step 1. Every new entry point (the `agents` and `agent-docs` commands, the dashboard route, writing into other tools' config folders) goes into `docs/security-architecture.md` in the same change. Installing skills is always opt-in, never silent. Changing the skills means running the agent sandbox, or writing the skill review (§3.3).

tasks.name: Remove atm run; atm claim hold keeps a claim alive instead
tasks.description:
atm must not be able to run commands (the user's security decision, 2026-11-06): `atm run <id> -- <command>` (`loop run` in the new tree) goes. Today a permission prompt covers the whole line, but once `atm run *` is allowed, any command runs through it unchecked. What it gave, a claim kept alive during a long command (a test suite, a wait on CI), comes from a new `atm claim hold <id>` that runs nothing.

## `claim hold <id>`
- The agent writes `atm claim hold T-1 && npm test` in one Bash call. `claim hold` renews the claim once, starts a detached watcher and returns at once; the shell then runs the command itself. atm never sees it.
- The watcher follows the shell that called `claim hold` (its parent process): it renews the claim at the usual interval (three times per lease) while that process lives, and exits when it is gone. It checks the process's start time as well as its ID, so a reused ID doesn't keep it going.
- It stops after a cap (default 4 hours, `--max` to change it within bounds), and when the claim is released, finished or taken over. It renews only that claim, as that agent, and never fails loudly: an error ends the watcher, and the claim then lapses as usual.
- `--json` prints the claim and the watcher's PID and cap.

## Remove
`loop run` and its code (the child process, the renewal loop, exit-code passing), its tests, and its mentions in the skills (`do-task`, `loop-tasks`, `push`), `plugin/CLAUDE.md` and the docs (`docs/improving-atm-cli-ergonomics.md`, `docs/v4/atm-cli.md`, `docs/security-architecture.md`).

## Security
`docs/security-architecture.md`: atm runs no command an agent or a task text passes it, as an invariant with its check (a test that the command tree has no command taking a command to run). The watcher runs nothing and only writes claims; record it as such. Skills change, so the written skill review (§3.3).

## Tests
Scenarios or `claims.test.mjs`: `claim hold` renews while its parent lives and stops when it exits; it stops at the cap; it stops when the claim is released; a reused PID with another start time doesn't count. The changelog and What's new entries go with T-425's release.

notes.text: atm loop run removed; atm claim hold <id> (watcher follows the calling shell by pid+start time, --max 240 min). I24 + static check. Review: the watcher (cli/claims.py), skill wording.

tasks.name: Review decisions as their own commands; guarded exits from review; one skip
tasks.description:
Agreed with the user (2026-11-06). A review decision changes no state; the exits from review need the right decision. T-425 already moved approve and request-changes out of `task state` into `atm task review approve|request-changes <id>`; this finishes the model.

## Review decisions: `atm task review <decision> <id>`
The decision comes before the ID, so a permission prefix tells them apart.
- `approve <id> [--note]`, `review_state: approved`
- `request-changes <id> --reason`, `review_state: changes_requested`
- `reject <id> --reason`, `review_state: rejected` (new)

All three only on a task in review, and the task stays in review. **No skill pre-approves any of them:** they are the user's, and an agent asking for one gets a permission prompt the user answers.

## The exits from review, guarded in atm (`atm-cli/atm/lib/state.py`)
| Decision | Exit (`task state <id> …`) |
|---|---|
| `approved` | `done` |
| `changes_requested` | `in_progress` (its agent first, as now) |
| `rejected` | `todo` (back to the pool, the work dropped) or `skipped` |

Without the matching decision, atm refuses the exit, for an agent and a person alike: nobody passes, reworks or drops a review without the decision. The old `reject` transition (review to todo in one step) goes; `task state <id> todo` from review is the rejected exit.

## One skip
`skipped` from any open state (todo, blocked, in progress, in review; from review only once rejected), with `--resolution wont_do|obsolete|duplicate` and `--duplicate-of`; it releases the claim. `done` loses `--resolution`: done means the work is done.

## Update
- the skills (`do-task`, `loop-tasks`, `close-sprint`: an approval or a rejection is something the user runs, e.g. `! atm task review approve T-1`; no skill pre-approves `task review`), `plugin/CLAUDE.md`, `docs/task-states.md` (the diagram), `docs/improving-atm-cli-ergonomics.md`
- `docs/security-architecture.md`: I23 rests on atm's guards (the exits need the decision) and on no skill pre-approving `task review`; its check becomes the scenarios plus `skills.test.ts`
- the dashboard where it shows `review_state` (a `rejected` label)
- the skill review (§3.3), and the changelog with T-425's release

## Tests
Scenarios: each decision, refused outside review; each exit refused without its decision and allowed with it (an agent and a person); skip from each open state, from review only when rejected; done without `--resolution`. `skills.test.ts`: no skill pre-approves `task review`.

notes.text: task review approve|request-changes|reject; exits guarded in atm for everyone (done=approved, todo/skip=rejected, start=rework); skip from any open state; done has no --resolution. Review: state.py guards, cross-worktree record.

tasks.description:
Installing the skills ([better-way-to-distribute-atm.md](docs/better-way-to-distribute-atm.md) §3, §5), in the Python atm, **for Claude Code only**; built so other harnesses are an entry in a table later (T-413).

## Change
- `atm agents install [--harness claude] [--project] [--copy]`: writes the skills of this atm's version to `~/.agentic-task-manager/skills/` and links them into `~/.claude/skills/` (or the project's `.claude/skills/` with `--project`), Claude Code's copy with `allowed-tools`; `--copy` copies instead. Idempotent; prints every path it wrote.
- `atm agents status`: per harness in the table (Claude Code for now), where atm's skills are (linked, copied, missing, stale) and their version.
- `atm agents uninstall`: removes exactly what install wrote, nothing else.
- Harnesses are a table (name, how to detect it, its folders, link or copy, extra frontmatter), so adding `~/.agents/skills/` and the others later touches only the table.
- Opt-in only: never run by atm on its own. The new entry point (writing into another tool's folder) in [security-architecture.md](docs/security-architecture.md).

## Tests
`tests/scripts/agents.test.mjs` on a temporary home: install, status, re-install (no change), copy mode, uninstall leaves nothing, a stale link reported.

notes.text: `atm agents install|status|uninstall` (Claude Code; harness table in `lib/agents.py`): links from `~/.claude/skills`, copies with `--copy`/`--project`, record in `agents.json`, never replaces a folder it didn’t write. Review: the security entry; opt-in only.

tasks.name: Rust: the model, reading the store, task details
tasks.description:
Slice 2a of [porting-to-rust.md](docs/porting-to-rust.md) §5 (step 2, split in four: this, then `task list`, `task deps` and `project status`). Follows the [Rust guide](docs/guides/rust.md); the Python atm is the spec (§1: `--json` identical, text the same or better, exit codes identical).

## Change
- `atm-common`: the model the reads need (task, sprint, release, component, the vocabularies and kinds from `atm-cli/atm/common/schema/vocabularies.json`, the errors), with `serde` keeping atm's key order (§3).
- `atm-db`: reading `.agentic-task-manager/tasks.json` and `tasks-archive.json` as the Python store does (`db/jsongit/`: finding the folder, refusing symlinks, the in-memory upgrades of older files), behind a store interface.
- `atm-lib`: the reads `task details` uses (`lib/tasks.py`'s `show_tasks`).
- `atm-boot`: opening a project from the current directory or `--dir`.
- `atm-cli`: the layout the later slices fill: `src/main.rs` with only the root `Cli` (clap derive), the global options (`-j/--json`, `--dir`, anywhere on the line as today), the dispatch and the exit codes; `src/commands/<group>.rs` per top-level command (`task` here; `version` moves to `meta.rs`); `task details <id>...` as text and `--json`, with Python's error messages (unknown task, no task file).

## Tests
Unit tests in the crates; the `task details` scenarios (and the error and global-option ones it makes pass) leave `tests/scripts/rust-expected-failures.json`.

notes.text: Model and vocabulary checks (`atm-common`), strict read of `tasks.json` and the archive behind a `Store` trait plus a memory store (`atm-db`), `show_tasks` (`atm-lib`), `open_project` (`atm-boot`), `task details` text and `--json` with the `main.rs` + `commands/` layout (`atm-cli`); 9 tests off the expected list

tasks.name: Rust: the write path: the lock folder, the change transaction, the claims store
tasks.description:
Slice 3a of [porting-to-rust.md](docs/porting-to-rust.md) §5 (step 3, split in four: this, then the task states, `task review` and `loop next`): the store's write path, which every later slice writes through.

## Change
- `atm-db`: the task folder's **lock** as the Python atm has it (`db/jsongit/lock.py`): a lock folder with `owner.json`, waited for up to `ATM_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, broken when its owner is dead or it is over a minute old, released on exit and on SIGTERM; the same folder, so the Python and the Rust atm can run against one project during the switch (`lock.test.mjs`, and `atm _lock-test`). `porting-to-rust.md` §3 says `std::fs::File::lock`: correct it to the lock folder.
- `atm-db`: the **claims store** (`db/jsongit/claims.py`): where it is (shared by a clone's worktrees), reading it, writing it atomically.
- `atm-db`: the **change transaction** (`JsonGitStore.change`, `db/working.py`): under the lock, read `tasks.json` and the claims store, let the change run, write only what changed (`tasks.json` only when its text changed, with the archive first when tasks move into it), atomically, as `to_json` + newline.
- `atm-lib`: the change's actor and time (`ATM_NOW`, `ATM_AGENT` / the session) as later slices need them.

## Tests
Unit tests for the lock (two holders, a dead owner, an old lock, the timeout) and for writing only what changed; `lock.test.mjs` leaves `tests/scripts/rust-expected-failures.json`.

notes.text: The write path in Rust: the lock folder (Python’s protocol, SIGTERM-safe via `signal-hook`, owner checks via `sysinfo`), the claims store and its snapshot, the change transaction (`Store::change`, `Working`), `atm _lock-test`; `lock.test.mjs` passes (6 off the list); porting doc §3 corrected

tasks.name: Rust: task add and task note
tasks.description:
Slice 5a of [porting-to-rust.md](docs/porting-to-rust.md) §5 (step 5, split in four: this, then `task edit`, the `sprint` group, and the `release`, `component` and `project` groups), on T-445's write path.

## Change
- `task add` (`lib/edit.py`'s `add_new_tasks`): one task from options, or many from `--json-file` (a list, or `{"tasks": [...]}`), placeholder IDs (`new-1`) replaced by the next IDs in the project's pattern and followed in dependencies; the whole file refused, nothing written, for an unknown type or priority, an invalid label, an unknown or closed sprint, a dependency that doesn't exist or a cycle; `created_by`, timestamps, the components a task's files suggest (SR-2.7); text and `--json` as in Python.

The `task add` and `task note` scenarios (`add.json`, `notes.json`, …) and `add.test.mjs` (eight agents adding at once) leave `tests/scripts/rust-expected-failures.json`.

tasks.name: Rust: atm-vcs and the vcs group
tasks.description:
Slice 6a of [porting-to-rust.md](docs/porting-to-rust.md) §5 (step 6, split in three: this, then the merge driver, and the `db` group with `doctor`): `atm-vcs`, running git (the Python atm's `vcs/git.py`), and the `vcs` group (`lib/code.py`, `cli/commands/vcs.py`).

## Change
- `atm-vcs`: the version control behind a project (checked-out branch, user name, default base, remote URL, the files a commit stages, refusing whatever would stage more than the files named).
- `vcs commit <id> --file … [--dir …]` (the task's files plus the store's, the workflow's commit template and trailers, the commit recorded on the task, refusing a file in another agent's claimed task), `vcs pr <id>… --number --url`, `vcs pushed --pr N --at` (merges recorded, a planned release released when all its tasks are merged), `vcs repository [URL] [--from]` (the web address from a remote, PR links moved); text and `--json` as in Python.

## Tests
The `commit`, `pr`, `pushed` and `repository` scenarios and `git.test.mjs` leave `tests/scripts/rust-expected-failures.json`.

notes.text: Rust `atm-vcs` and `vcs commit|pr|pushed|repository`; split with T-475 (merge driver) and T-476 (db group, doctor); 31 tests left the list (163 left).

tasks.name: Rust: atm serve itself: the server, its record, the registry, the page and its headers
tasks.description:
Slice 7a of [porting-to-rust.md](docs/porting-to-rust.md) §5 (step 7, split in three: this, then the read API and the project's files): `atm serve` itself, in `atm-api` on axum/tokio (§3), as the Python atm's `cli/serve.py` and `api/server.py` run it.

## Change
- `atm serve start|stop|status` and `atm service [--refresh] [--port] [--open] [--all] [--dir]`: one detached server per user (`ATM_HOME`), started as the `atm` binary itself, its record (pid, port, build, version) in `ATM_HOME`, a busy port moving to the next, a stale record cleaned up, `stop` ending only the recorded server (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL), two starts at once starting one server, `--refresh` restarting an older or rebuilt dashboard on the same port; `/__atm/whoami`.
- The **registry** of projects (`db/registry.py`, `projects.json`): adding a project when a command runs in it, IDs from `meta.id` (another when it is taken), `meta.dashboard.listed`.
- The **Host check** (DNS rebinding), `[::1]` and `127.0.0.1` both, and the security headers and CSP of [security-architecture.md](docs/security-architecture.md) I12–I13.
- The dashboard page, from `plugin/templates/tasks-dashboard.html`, embedded at build and served from memory at each of its paths (T-429's routes); CompMD's runtime from `plugin/assets/compmd/`, at `/assets/`, read-only.
- New dependencies: `axum` and `tokio` (named in §3).

## Tests
The `serve.test.mjs` tests about the server's lifecycle, the page, the headers and the Host check leave `tests/scripts/rust-expected-failures.json`.

tasks.name: Windows: the stress test (16 agents in two worktrees) fails
tasks.description:
Found in T-480 on `dev/0.33.0-switch`. `tests/scripts/stress.test.mjs` (16 concurrent agents in two worktrees) fails on CI's Windows runner and passes on Linux and macOS.

## What CI showed
- With atm's 10 s lock wait: agents time out waiting for the lock (`timed out waiting for the lock …/wt2/.agentic-task-manager/.lock`).
- With the test's lock wait raised to 60 s on Windows (decided with Hakan, `ATM_LOCK_TIMEOUT`): the test fails after 29 s, with the cleanup's `EPERM` on the test's folder, which hides the assertion underneath: some process still has the folder open.

## To find
- What still holds the folder: an atm process that outlives the test (a `claim hold` watcher not ending with its shell on Windows is a suspect: the same `EPERM` shows in `claims.test.mjs`'s watcher test), or a slow exit.
- Whether the lock is slow on Windows (git and process starts there are several times slower), and whether agents queue longer than they should.

## Done when
The test passes on CI's Windows runner, ideally at atm's default lock wait.

notes.text: Also on macOS CI, twice on 2026-11-08 (runs 42433227055 on `dev/0.33.0`, 42439602611 on `dev/0.32.0`), each passing on another run: agent-16 timed out on atm’s 10 s lock wait in `wt2`. So the lock queues too long under 16 agents on slow runners, not only on Windows.

The lock’s queue: the wait starts again when the lock changes hands (owner.json’s new token), up to 6× the wait; unit tests for both. The macOS CI timeout is this; the Windows run is checked in ATM-482 (the suite isn’t run on Windows CI until then), which also owns the EPERM (claim watcher).

tasks.name: The app's in-app updates (Tauri updater)
tasks.description:
The app checks for, downloads and installs its own updates through Tauri's updater plugin (agentic-status-bar, not a Tauri app, uses Sparkle: only its release habits carry over, not its mechanism).

## Change
- `tauri-plugin-updater`, its endpoint a `latest.json` update manifest attached to each GitHub release.
- The release workflow signs the app bundle with Tauri's updater key (a new secret, `TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY` and its password; separate from the Developer ID signature) and writes `latest.json`; the public key is built into the app.
- The app asks before installing; never updates silently. The bundled `atm` binary updates with it.
- A Homebrew cask install updates through `brew upgrade` instead (the cask says `auto_updates true`, or the updater is off for it: decide in the task).

## Docs
`packaging/README.md` (the secret, the manifest), `docs/security-architecture.md` (a new entry point: downloads and installs code).

## Tests
The manifest's generation, tested; the update flow checked by hand against a draft release.

With option B the bundled atm CLI updates with the app either way. I would suggest `auto_updates true`: one update path for everyone. → The app updates itself, in addition to brew upgrade: the cask says auto_updates true.

tasks.name: Release 0.33.0: atm as the Rust CLI only
tasks.description:
The first release without the plugin: `dev/0.33.0` to `main`, tagged, built, signed and published, with the formula and the first export of the skills to `solo-swe/skills`. The release process is in [packaging/README.md](packaging/README.md).

## On `dev/0.33.0`
- **Version:** `0.33.0` in `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package]`), and `Cargo.lock` after `cargo build`.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** the `[Unreleased]` entries become `## [0.33.0] - <date>`: T-453, T-454, T-477, T-478, T-480, and how plugin users move.
- **WHATS-NEW.md:** a `## [0.33.0]` entry, 3–6 plain bullets of at most 180 characters each (`release-notes.test.ts`): atm is now its own program (Homebrew or a download), its skills go into your agents with one command, and your projects and dashboard carry over.

- **Security checklist** (`docs/security-architecture.md` §3): the skills and `docs/agent/` changed, so do a written review of the skills in §3.3 instead of the live sandbox run. Check that the T-454 entry describes what shipped.
- **Checks:** `pnpm run verify` in `dashboard/`; `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo deny check` from the root.

## The PR
- Open it with `/atm-push`: `dev/0.33.0` to `main`. The ruleset's required checks (the three Rust jobs, lint and unit tests, Playwright) must pass.
- The user merges it, or says to merge it. Then record the merge (`atm vcs pushed --pr <n> --at <mergedAt>`).

## The release (with the user's go-ahead)

- Check the draft (six assets: five archives and `SHA256SUMS`), then publish it.
- Watch the Homebrew and Skills workflows. This is the Skills workflow's first run: check `solo-swe/skills` for the `skills/atm-*` folders and the `atm-v0.33.0` tag.

tasks.name: A release whose tasks merge in several PRs is never released
tasks.description:
`atm vcs pushed --pr <n>` releases a planned release only when **all** its tasks are merged **in that PR** (`release_with_merge` in [code.rs](crates/atm-lib/src/code.rs)). Release 0.32.0's sprint, *The Rust port*, merged in two PRs: #39 (32 tasks), then #40 (the other 5, which shipped in 0.33.0). Recording #39 said `0.32.0 stays planned: T-453, … are not merged in PR #39`, and recording #40 said the same about #39's 32 tasks. So 0.32.0 stays planned although every one of its tasks is merged.

## Change
- A release is released when every one of its tasks is merged (`merged_at` set), whichever PR merged it. Its release time is the last merge. The message names the tasks that keep it planned because they aren't merged yet, not because they merged in another PR.
- `atm vcs pushed` releases such a release the next time it runs. `atm doctor` (or `atm release list`) points out a planned release whose tasks are all merged, so this repo's 0.32.0 can be fixed by running it again.

## Tests
A scenario in `tests/scripts/scenarios/`: a release whose tasks are in two PRs stays planned after the first merge and is released by the second; a release with one PR still works as it does now.

notes.text: A release is released once all its tasks are merged, in any PR (released_at its last merge); messages say "not merged yet"; atm doctor warns about a planned release whose tasks are all merged. Scenarios in pr.json and releases.json. This repo’s 0.32.0 is released by `atm vcs pushed --pr 40` once this atm is installed.

tasks.name: Review and refactor the CI jobs from what the Rust port taught us
tasks.description:
Go through `.github/workflows/` with the user and propose changes, based on what CI did during *The Rust port* and the first releases. Each change is agreed first: editing CI is the user's call.

## What to look at
- **What runs when:** pushes to a release branch run nothing unless dispatched (`gh workflow run CI --ref <branch>`); a PR runs again after every push. Is that still the right trade?
- **Time and caching:** a run takes about 4–5 minutes. Look at the cargo and pnpm caches, the jobs that build the dashboard and atm more than once (Rust ×3, `atm for the e2e suite`, Playwright), and whether artifacts could be shared instead.
- **The app (T-455 onwards)** is part of `cargo build`/`test`, so the Linux job needs the webview's system packages and Windows builds against WebView2. See what that adds to each job, and whether the e2e binary and the release should build only `-p atm-cli`.
- **Windows:** the suite runs only partly there (T-480, T-482), and the stress test fails (T-481). Decide what the Windows job checks until those are done.
- **macOS:** the stress test hit lock timeouts twice (T-481). Is that a slow runner or a real bug?
- **Screenshots:** CI makes missing Linux baselines, and the local scripts get a Linux atm (T-485). Check that the two use the same binary and the same steps.
- **Runner images:** `ubuntu-latest` moves to Ubuntu 26 (CI's annotation); the e2e binary is built on 22.04 for an older glibc. Pin the images we depend on.
- **Required checks:** the ruleset names jobs by their display names (`Rust (ubuntu-latest)`, …), so renaming a job breaks merges. Keep the names in one place, or test that `.github/rulesets/main.json` matches `ci.yml` (`ci-workflow.test.ts`).
- **Release workflows:** `release.yml`, `homebrew.yml` and `skills.yml` worked first time for 0.32.0 and 0.33.0. Note anything worth keeping in `packaging/README.md`.

## Outcome
The agreed changes in the workflows, `ci-workflow.test.ts` and `AGENTS.md`'s CI section, with `docs/security-architecture.md` updated if a permission or secret changes.

tasks.name: Overhaul atm's human-readable output: alignment, grouping and styling
tasks.description:
atm's plain output (without `--json`) is hard to scan. For example, `atm project status` prints the per-sprint, per-type and per-label counts as one long comma-separated line each, and the blocked and waiting lists as long lines joined with `;`. Make it read well in a terminal without changing what it says or what `--json` returns.

## First, a design with the user
Propose the look before changing code: a before/after of `atm project status`, `atm task list`, `atm task details`, `atm sprint list`, `atm release list` and `atm doctor`. Decide:
- **Alignment:** columns padded to the widest value (IDs, statuses, priorities), long names cut or wrapped to the terminal's width, and sections with a heading and indented lines instead of `a, b, c` runs.
- **Styling:** bold headings, colour for status kinds and priorities, dimmed secondary text. Only when standard output is a terminal; never with `NO_COLOR`, `--json`, or output going to a pipe or file.
- **What `project status` leads with:** the active sprint and what's next first; the long breakdowns (all sprints, types, labels) shorter, or behind a flag.
- **Dependencies:** terminal width and colour either hand-written or from a crate (e.g. `anstyle`, already in the tree through clap). Any new crate is proposed first.

## Agents read this output too
The skills relay what atm prints, and agents act on it. Keep it plain text when it isn't a terminal, keep each fact on a line agents can find, and check `docs/agent/` and the skills that quote output. A change to output agents act on follows AGENTS.md's security checklist (the written review in `docs/security-architecture.md` §3.3).

## Tests
The scenarios' exact `stdout` expectations change with the new layout: update them in one place per command. Add a test that a pipe gets no escape codes and that `NO_COLOR` turns colour off.

tasks.name: ADR-003: workspaces, the set of projects atm works on
tasks.description:
A design proposal, as an ADR, for a **workspace**: a set of projects atm works on, of which there may be several (usually one; others for tests, or work and personal projects).

## Why
The logic that works across projects (the project list with summaries, worktrees and logos; search across projects; skipping a broken project) lives in atm-api's HTTP routes, and the app (T-456) needs the same. atm-lib knows only one project; the registry is concrete in atm-db; boot is a bag of openers and JSON-in-git helpers ([layered-architecture.md](docs/layered-architecture.md) §3.2, §5.1, §11.2).

## The ADR
- Research: how atm's layers handle one project and many today; what the registry, `ATM_HOME`, `atm service`, the dashboard's routes and the app assume; how other tools model workspaces.
- Propose the workspace: what it is and holds, how one is chosen (default, `ATM_HOME`, a flag), the API's place for it (`api/v<N>/workspace/…`), the layers that own it, and how boot gets simpler.
- Diagrams in Mermaid. Options with trade-offs, a recommendation, consequences and a migration plan.

Reviewed with Hakan; T-456 waits for it.

Four questions for the review at the end.
Approved: Approved in Crit after one round (the task folder is the store’s, not the model’s)

Mermaid diagrams in the app need it (T-502).

## Steps (§4.7)
1. **A check first, in a branch:** the plugin's smallest form, in `cargo run -p atm-app` and `cargo tauri dev`. Does WebKit let the opaque-origin frame load modules from `compmd://localhost` with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`? Does Tauri leave the scheme's responses alone? 2. **Decide with Hakan (§4.6):** the plugin as a crate of its own in atm's workspace (`crates/tauri-plugin-compmd/`, no atm dependencies) until CompMD ships one.
3. **The change (§4.1, §4.2):** the plugin (embedded folder, path checks, H1/H2 headers, 404/405 with reasons); the app's CSP names `compmd://localhost` and `http://compmd.localhost`, `frame-ancestors 'none'` back, `devCsp` only adds the CLI's socket; the dashboard gives CompMD a full `base` in the app (`convertFileSrc('', 'compmd')`).
4. **Nothing fails silently (§4.3):** `CompMd.svelte` listens for the view's `error` event and shows a note at the block; a failed `compmd.js` load shows a note on the text; both log the cause.

## Tests (§4.5)
The plugin's handler; the app's policy; no IPC from `compmd:`; atm serve and the plugin on the same header table; the page's error notes; by hand in a window, both `cargo tauri dev` and `cargo run -p atm-app`, with T-502's test diagrams and Help.

tasks.name: CompMD's files from compmd:// after an upgrade: WebKit's custom-scheme cache
tasks.description:
A gap in [ADR-004](docs/adr/ADR-004-compmd-in-tauri-through-its-own-protocol.md): WebKit (WKWebView, on macOS and iOS) caches a custom URI scheme's responses, so a file replaced at the same path can keep running its old version (seen in another Tauri app's custom-scheme frames). ADR-004 keeps the paths CompMD's files have under `atm serve` (`/assets/compmd/<version>/…`). The CompMD version in the path changes with CompMD, but not when atm rebuilds the same CompMD version differently (its packs, `compmd.config.json`, a pack's built module), so after an atm upgrade the app could run the previous files from `compmd://`, and the page and its frames could speak different versions of the frame protocol.

## 1. Check it first
In the running app on macOS (`cargo run -p atm-app`, and a bundle): open a task with a diagram; replace a CompMD file the plugin serves (a frame's `runtime.js`, or the Mermaid pack's module) with a changed copy at the same path, one that shows it changed (a console line); rebuild, run again, open the task: does the old file still run? Record what each build showed.

## 2. If it does, fix it in `tauri-plugin-compmd`, as the plugin's default
The plugin is meant to move into CompMD for any Tauri host (ADR-004 decision 5), so the fix is its default behaviour, not atm's configuration. One of:
- **Content-hashed paths:** the plugin serves the build's CompMD folder under a name made from a hash of its files, gives the page that `base` (H4), and answers with `Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable`; a changed file is then a new path;
- **or, if the paths must stay as under `atm serve`:** `Cache-Control: no-cache` with a validator (an `ETag` and `If-None-Match`, as `atm serve` sends) that WebKit honours for custom schemes; check in the app that it does.
Prefer the first if WebKit's handling of validators on custom schemes is uncertain.

## 3. Record it
- ADR-004: the result in its Risks; a decision if the plugin changes (and the design doc's §4.2 if its headers change).
- The plugin's header tests stay in step with `atm serve`'s (H1, H2: CORS `*`, `nosniff`, `sandbox allow-scripts` on frame documents); if the cache headers differ between the two, say why in both.

notes.text: Scope after T-503 (ADR-005): the frames are CompMD’s plugin’s, at content-hashed paths, so the cache can’t serve an old frame. What is left to check is atm’s own atm: scheme (assets.rs: compmd.js, its WebAssembly, the packs’ modules, at /assets/compmd/<version>/, no-cache). A stale pack module fails its hash check visibly; check compmd.js across a rebuild of the same CompMD version, and if it sticks, name the folder by a hash.

Checked on macOS 26: two app builds with different compmd.js at the same atm: path each ran their own, so WebKit doesn’t cache atm: responses (no-cache honoured) and the paths stay; recorded in ADR-005 Risks. Found and fixed on the way: the pack’s module was fetched from the page origin (tauri://), refused by connect-src; moduleUrl puts it on atm:.

## On `dev/0.34.0`
- **Version:** `0.34.0` in `Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package]`, which the app takes too), and `Cargo.lock` after `cargo build`.
- **CHANGELOG.md:** the `[Unreleased]` entries become `## [0.34.0] - <date>`. Check the T-503 entry says what shipped: the plugin and the error notes are in, diagrams in the app wait for CompMD 0.6.0 (0.35.0).
- **WHATS-NEW.md:** a `## [0.34.0]` entry, 3–6 plain bullets of at most 180 characters each (`release-notes.test.ts`): the atm app for macOS (install with Homebrew, it brings its own `atm`), its icon, your projects carried over to the new state folder, and that diagrams in the app come in the next release.
- **Screenshots:** regenerate the Linux baselines once (`pnpm run test:e2e:visual:update`, Docker), and look at the ones that changed.
- **Security checklist** (`docs/security-architecture.md` §3): `skills/atm-push`, `skills/atm-serve`, `skills/claude-code.json` and `docs/agent/commands.md` changed since `main`, so a written review of them in §3.3 instead of the live sandbox run. New entry points this release (the app's commands, deep links, the `compmd:` scheme) are in I25 and I26: check they describe what shipped.
- **Checks:** `pnpm run verify` in `dashboard/`; `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo deny check` from the root.

## The PR
- Open it with `/atm-push`: `dev/0.34.0` to `main`. The required checks must pass.

tasks.name: The atm app's UI overhaul: a desktop app, not the web page in a window
tasks.description:
The app shows the dashboard's web page as it is in a browser. Make it feel like a desktop app (Hakan).

## What it could have
- **The title in the title bar:** the page's header (project, workspace) goes into the window's title bar (Tauri's overlay title bar on macOS), not a second bar under it.
- **Tabs:** several projects (or workspaces, the board) open at once, one tab each.
- **A collapsible side panel** listing the workspace's projects, instead of the project selector.
- **A proper status bar:** what the dashboard's footer shows now (version, connection, agents at work, the active sprint), as the app's own.
- **Menus:** the app's menu bar (macOS) for settings, the views, the projects and workspaces, Help and What's new, with their keyboard shortcuts; settings in a window or sheet of their own.
- Anything else a desktop app should have that the page lacks (window state kept between runs, the Dock menu, …).

## First: a design, with Hakan
A short design document (`docs/`): what changes in the app and what stays shared with the browser dashboard (one Svelte code base: the browser keeps working as it does), which Tauri APIs it uses (window, menu, title bar), how tabs map to the dashboard's addresses and deep links (T-459), and how it fits T-506 (no refresh settings). Review it with Hakan, then break it into tasks with `/atm-create-tasks`.

## Checks
The Tauri guide's by-hand check in a window (`cargo tauri dev` and `cargo run -p atm-app`), the app e2e specs, and the security doc where a new command or capability is added (I25).

tasks.name: Desktop app: windows and the shell (subscriptions by window, shell, open_window, set_title)
tasks.description:
Step 1 of [the desktop app design](docs/app-desktop-ui-design.md) (§9, accepted in T-510): the groundwork for several windows and the page's own shell. **No visible change yet.**

## Change

- **Subscriptions belong to a window:** `AppState` keeps them by the webview's label; `unwatch_all` becomes `unwatch_window` (a page loading again ends only its own window's), and a window closing ends its own.

- The page: a small `lib/app-shell.ts` (or beside `lib/api/`) reading `shell` once, for the later steps.

Step 4 of [the desktop app design](docs/app-desktop-ui-design.md) ([§3](docs/app-desktop-ui-design.md#3-tabs)). Decided: a tab is an **address**, one page and one dashboard state per window, not a state per tab.

- **The strip** in the title bar: each tab its project's logo and name (or the page's title), the needs-you count, a close button; drag to reorder; `+`, ⌘T and File ▸ New Tab open the workspace's overview.
- **Switching** (a click, ⌃Tab / ⌃⇧Tab, ⌘⇧] / ⌘⇧[) navigates to the tab's address through `lib/navigation.ts`; the tab keeps its address, the preferences keep the rest.

A switch between two tabs of a large project within the e2e budget (200 ms, `tests/e2e/performance.spec.ts`). If it isn't, keep the last few projects' data in `state.svelte.ts` (a cache), not a state per tab.

Add the timing to [the performance spec](dashboard/tests/e2e/performance.spec.ts), beside its `switching tabs` test, with the same budget (`BUDGET_MS`: 200 ms locally, twice that in CI).

## Change
- In the app (`tasksServer.asApp()`), with the `large-500` fixture and a second project: open tabs on the Kanban, the List and the Graph of the large project and on the second project, then time each `.title-bar-tab` click until its page is shown (its view's first card or node visible, the title the tab's project), as the spec times its views.
- Also time ⌃Tab (the menu's Next Tab, `chooseMenu({ kind: 'next_tab' })`) once round the tabs.
- Log the timings as the other tests do (`tab switch in the app (ms):`) and expect each under `BUDGET_MS`.

## If it is over budget
Measure where the time goes (`--trace on` locally) and fix the cause; never raise the budget (AGENTS.md, Performance budgets). Record the timings in T-514's follow-up note on this task.

notes.text: Timed the app’s tabs on 500 tasks (performance.spec.ts): same-project switches 45–110 ms; back from another project was 240–290 ms, over budget. Fixed: the graph keeps the last 4 layouts (dagre ~100 ms), the hidden Graph and List are not drawn (List mounted only while shown). Now 140–200 ms with the mock’s ~55 ms transport; List switch 108–175; reloads faster. Specs that read hidden views open them. Close to the budget under the full local suite: watch it.

tasks.name: Desktop app: the update shows its download's progress, and the app restarts by itself after installing
tasks.description:
Found in T-522 (0.35.0 updating to 0.36.0): after the click, the app sat on "Installing…" with no sign of progress while it downloaded the 33 MB archive, and it did not reopen on the new version: it was installed, and Hakan closed the app himself.

Send the page the downloaded and total bytes on a channel the command takes, and "installing" once the download is done; `UpdateNotice` shows a progress bar and the step (downloading, installing, restarting).
- **The restart:** find why `app.restart()` didn't bring the app back after the install on macOS (the single-instance plugin, the window-state writes on exit from T-518, or the restart racing the bundle's replacement), and fix it; if a restart can't be made reliable, the notice says the update is installed and offers Restart Now.
- A failure at any step still says why, and the running app stays as it is.

## Tests
Unit and e2e (`app.spec.ts`, the IPC mock sending progress); the restart by hand on macOS at the next release, with Hakan (as T-522).

Progress on a channel (`install_update` sends bytes every 256 KB, then installing); the notice shows Downloading… X of Y MB with a bar, Installing…, Restarting…. tasks.name: Mark a release released by hand: atm release edit --released
tasks.description:
A release becomes `released` only when `atm vcs pushed` finds every one of its tasks merged in a PR. A release with a task that has no commit (a check done with the user, such as T-521 for 0.35.0 and T-522 for 0.36.0) never does: 0.32.0, 0.35.0 and 0.36.0 still show `planned` though they are out. There is no command to say so by hand.

## Change
- `atm release edit <id> --released [YYYY-MM-DD]` marks the release released, on the date given (today without one); `--planned` takes it back. It says which of its tasks are not done or not merged, and goes ahead (the user's call), unless a task is still open (to do, in progress, in review, blocked), which it refuses unless `--force`.
- `atm release list` and the dashboard's release view show a release marked by hand as released, with its date.
- `docs/agent/` (the release commands) and the release steps in `packaging/README.md` say to run it after publishing, when a release holds such a task.

## Tests
A scenario in `tests/scripts/scenarios/` (mark, unmark, the refusal for an open task and `--force`, the list's line), and atm-lib's unit tests for the rule.

notes.text: `atm release edit <id> --released [YYYY-MM-DD]` (today without a date) and `--planned` (atm-lib `mark_release`): names the tasks done but not merged; refuses while one is open unless `--force`. `atm release list` and the dashboard already show a released release with its date. Seven scenarios and a unit test; docs/agent/commands.md and packaging/README.md (step 5).

tasks.name: Design: two task IDs (a UUID and a project key, ATM-123) and dependencies across projects
tasks.description:
Hakan wants tasks to have two IDs, as JIRA does: a **UUID** for technical reasons, and a **key** for people, a project prefix and a number instead of `T-`: `ASB-001` (Agentic Status Bar), `ATM-001` (Agentic Task Manager), `FIG-001` (Fig), `LFB-001` (Learn Forever Blog). Keys let a task refer to another project's: `LFB-005` blocked by `ATM-978`.

Design it with Hakan, as an ADR replacing the current ID scheme (`docs/adr/`), then break the work into tasks with `/atm-create-tasks`.

## To settle
- **The two IDs:** `uid` (a UUID, never shown, never changed) and the key (`ATM-978`); the prefix in `meta` (e.g. `meta.key`), chosen at `atm db init`, unique across the workspace's projects; keys unique within the project. Which one the files, the API, the app's commands and the dashboard's addresses use.
- **Migration:** `atm db migrate` gives each task a UUID and rekeys `T-527` as `ATM-527`, keeping the numbers; dependencies, `related`, notes, commit trailers, PR records and links follow. Old IDs stay resolvable as aliases (commit messages and PRs say `T-527`). The archive too.
- **Merges and parallel agents:** the merge driver matches tasks by UUID; two branches that both add a task never collide, and the key of one is renumbered on merge (as today's driver renumbers).
- **Across projects:** a dependency or `related` entry naming another project's key, resolved through the workspace's projects (`projects.json`): its status shown, an unfinished one an unmet dependency for the loop; a project missing, renamed or rekeyed; the dashboard's link to it; `atm doctor`'s checks. Reading another project's task folder is a new entry point (`docs/security-architecture.md`).
- **Where IDs show:** the CLI and `atm docs`, the dashboard (cards, links, the graph, addresses), the app, commit templates and `atm vcs` parsing (`code.rs`'s mention of a task ID), the skills.

## Output
The ADR, reviewed with Hakan, and the implementation tasks (data model, migrate, merge driver, cross-project resolution, dashboard, docs, skills), added through `/atm-create-tasks`.

notes.text: Draft ADR-007 for Hakan’s review: UUID ids, keys from meta.key, provisional keys until on the base branch, merges by UUID, prefix migration, references across projects. Once approved: the implementation tasks via /atm-create-tasks.

tasks.name: Task keys: the migration (atm db migrate) and atm project key set
tasks.description:
ADR-007 §6.

## The first migration (`atm db migrate`)
Every task, archived ones too: a UUID, its number from the ID's trailing digits (an ID that doesn't fit the file's prefix gets the next free number and keeps its old ID as an alias), references rewritten to UUIDs (`dependencies`, `related`, notes pointing at a task, claims keyed by UUID), `meta.key` from the name's initials when they make 3 to 6 letters (else the old prefix), the old prefix into `meta.key_history`, every task final, the format version set. Says what it did.

## `atm project key set <KEY>`
Sets `meta.key`, pushes the old one onto `meta.key_history`; numbers and references unchanged. Warns (doesn't refuse) when another project in the user's workspaces uses the key. `atm db init` asks for a key on a new project, suggesting the initials.

## Tests
Scenarios: migrate a file with dependencies, related, claims, an archive and an odd ID; then `key set` twice, and every old key still finds its task. A test that migrates a copy of this repository's own file and loses nothing.

notes.text: From T-538: atm 0.37 and older have no format check and would read a format-2 file as valid (UUIDs pass its ID rule) and give new tasks T- IDs. Guard: the migration should make the file unreadable to them, or the skills’ version check (T-547) require 0.38.0. Also ADR-007 §2/§6 give TaskMan as an example, which is 7 letters, over the 3–6 rule: fix the example.

atm db migrate --keys (opt-in until T-543): UUIDs v8 from meta.id + old ID (same in every clone), numbers kept (others above next_id, old ID an alias), references, sprint reports and claims rewritten, meta.key from the name, old prefix in key_history, all final. atm project key show|set (warns on a key another registered project uses). Unit tests, keys.test.mjs (incl. this repo’s own file, nothing lost); ADR-007 updated.

tasks.name: Task keys: the merge driver matches by UUID and moves only provisional numbers

- Same `number` on two tasks: the provisional one takes the next free number (above both sides and `meta.next_number`), of two provisional ones the incoming side's; its old key goes into `aliases`. Two final ones: a conflict, never a guess.
- No reference rewriting (they are UUIDs); `meta.next_number` merges as the larger.
- A side still in the old format is migrated first (as phases became sprints), so a branch from before the migration merges.
- `next_free_id` goes.

## Tests
Real git merges in `tests/scripts/merge.test.mjs`: both add a task; provisional vs final; two final (conflict); an old-format side.

notes.text: Merge driver: an old-format side (base too) is migrated first when another is keyed, so pre-migration branches merge task by task; keyed: one UUID added differently on both is a conflict; number clashes: final keeps it, of two provisional ours does, the mover takes the next free number with its old key as alias; two final: conflict, both kept; next_number the larger. next_free_id stays for legacy files until T-543. Unit tests and two real git merges.

Scenarios with two projects in a workspace: a dependency across them blocks the loop until done; the other project removed or unregistered; doctor's report.

tasks.name: The app: external links (About, Help, repository, PRs) open in the browser
tasks.description:
In the atm app, clicking a link in the About dialog does nothing (Hakan, 2026-11-16). The page's external links are plain `<a href target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">` anchors, which the app's webview doesn't open, and the app has no command or plugin that opens a link in the user's browser. So most likely **every** external link in the app is dead, not only the About dialog's: check each place first and list them in the outcome.

## Where the links are
`dialogs/AboutDialog.svelte` (source, CompMD), `ui/RepoRef.svelte` (commits, PRs), `overview/ProjectCard.svelte`, `kanban/KanbanColumns.svelte`, `progress/ReleaseView.svelte`, `shell/Footer.svelte`, `shell/ProjectTab.svelte`, `dialogs/WhatsNew.svelte`, `documents/DocumentViewer.svelte`, Help's links (rendered by CompMD: `docs/help.md`), and the Help ▸ CompMD menu item (`menu-actions.ts`, `page.open`).

## Change
- **One way to open an external link in the app**: the page hands `https:` (and `mailto:`) links to the app, which opens them in the system's browser; in the browser nothing changes. Prefer one place that catches every such link (a click handler on the document for external anchors, and `page.open`) over editing each component.
- **How the app opens them** is a choice to make first: Tauri's opener plugin (`tauri-plugin-opener`) is a **new dependency and needs Hakan's yes** before it is added (docs/guides/tauri.md, Platform features); the alternative is a small command of the app's own. Propose, don't add.
- **Only web addresses**: the app checks the URL itself (scheme `https`/`http`/`mailto` only, no `file:`, no custom schemes, no `atm:`), never trusts the page's; the capability allows only that command. Links inside rendered task text arrive from CompMD's sandbox as `link` events (compmd-rendering-design.md): they go through the same check.
- `docs/security-architecture.md`: opening a URL from the page is a new entry point (what is allowed, who checks it). `docs/guides/tauri.md` says how links open.

## Tests
Unit: the page sends external links to the app and keeps internal ones (`/projects/…`, `#…`) in the page; the app's check refuses other schemes (Rust test). e2e under `asApp()`: clicking the About dialog's source link and a commit link calls the app's command with the URL; in the browser the anchor stays `target="_blank"`. Then check by hand in a window (`cargo run -p atm-app`): About, Help ▸ CompMD, a PR link.

notes.text: Decided (Hakan, 2026-11-16): use Tauri’s opener plugin (`tauri-plugin-opener`), approved as a new dependency; pin it to a release at least two weeks old, as the other Tauri plugins are

External links in the app go through one command, `open_url` (app/src-tauri/src/external.rs): https/http with a host or mailto only, else refused; opened with `tauri-plugin-opener` =2.7.2 from Rust, the page has no opener permission. One capture handler in the layout catches every anchor; `page.open` too. Not checked in a real window: try About, Help ▸ CompMD and a PR link

tasks.name: ADR-008: other projects' tasks, referenced from any registered project and loaded when needed (replaces ADR-007 §7's wording)
tasks.description:
Write `docs/adr/ADR-008-…md` from [the freshness design](docs/cross-project-freshness-design.md) §4.1 (K4) and §9, as AGENTS.md asks for a decision that changes an ADR.

## What it decides
- **Any registered project** can be referenced, written by key or UUID; a key is looked up among every registered project, not only those of the workspaces the referring project is in (ADR-007 §7 said the latter; the code, `foreign::registered`, already does the former).
- **Loaded when needed, never watched:** another project is read when something needs it (readiness, display), through the stamp-keyed cache (design §5.1 B); only the open workspace's own projects are watched, for the app.
- **Worktree branches** (design §4.2): another project counts as its main working copy (V1).
- **The browser polls; the app is pushed** (design 1), and the store owns how it hears of changes (design §3).

## Also
ADR-007 gets a line under its status: "§7's lookup and freshness replaced by ADR-008". Link the design from both.

notes.text: ADR-008 written (any registered project referable, loaded when needed, never watched; the browser polls, the app is pushed; the store owns how it hears of changes; another project as its main copy). ADR-007 and the design point to it

tasks.name: Other projects' tasks: one stamp-keyed cache for the rules and the display
tasks.description:
[The freshness design](docs/cross-project-freshness-design.md) §5.1, option **B**: fixes P1, P4 and P5.

## The bug
`foreign::status` (the `ForeignStatus` hook the rules use: `waiting_for`, `ready`, unmet dependencies, the summary's `next` and board cards) remembers each answer for the whole process (`static SEEN`), so in `atm serve` and the app a task keeps reading "waiting on ATM-1" after ATM-1 is done, until a restart, while `derived.foreign` (T-549) shows it done and `atm loop next` takes it.

## Change (`crates/atm-lib/src/foreign.rs`)
- **One cache for the rules and the display**, keyed by the other project's `meta.id`: the project, its document and archive as read, and its store's `stamp()` (`tasks`, `archive`).
- **On each use**, compare the store's current stamp: unchanged → use the entry; changed → read the project again. Entries also **expire after a few seconds** (a constant, e.g. 5 s), against coarse file timestamps.
- `status`, `label`, `Lookup::view`, `find_uuid` and `resolve_in_other_project` all read through it; `registered()` is no longer opened per reference.
- The registry (which projects are registered, and where) is part of the key: a project removed from the workspaces, or its folder gone, is seen on the next use.
- Thread-safe (the server's threads): a `Mutex`, never held while reading a project.

## Tests
- **atm-lib:** in one process (no restart), after the other project's task is marked done, `status` and `Lookup::view` both say done, and a task depending on it is ready; an unchanged stamp doesn't re-read (count the reads); the entry expires; a removed project is `unregistered`.
- **The CLI suite (`serve.test.mjs`):** with a running `atm serve`, two registered projects: the other's task done → A's tasks route (without validators) gives `ready` true and no `waiting_for`; the overview's `next` follows.
- **The app (Rust command tests):** `project_tasks` within one `AppState` follows the other project's change.

notes.text: One cache for the rules and the display (`foreign.rs`), by registered folder, checked against the store’s `tasks`/`archive` stamp, 5 s expiry; the registry cached by its workspace files’ stamps; no lock held while reading. The workspace summary follows the projects it depends on. A long-running `atm serve` now shows another project’s done task as ready, without a restart. No app test (another agent had the app): it calls the same atm-lib

tasks.name: The tasks route's ETag also covers the projects a project's tasks reference
tasks.description:
[The freshness design](docs/cross-project-freshness-design.md) §5.3, option **D**: fixes P2 (the browser's stale 304).

## The bug
`api_tasks` (`crates/atm-api/src/routes.rs`) builds its ETag from the project's own `tasks` and `archive` stamps and the query. When only a referenced project changes, the browser's poll gets a 304 and keeps the old status, `ready` and `waiting_for`.

## Change
- **Which projects A references** (the `meta.id`s in its tasks' `dependencies`, `related` and `duplicate_of`, the archive too) is worked out on a full read and remembered by the server **keyed by A's stamp, never by time** (a new reference changes A's stamp, so it is never missed). atm-lib gives it (e.g. `Member::referenced_projects()`), atm-api only uses it.
- **The ETag** becomes A's stamp, the query, and the referenced projects' `tasks` and `archive` stamps (a project not found counts as null, so it appearing or going changes the tag too).
- A project with no references costs nothing extra; one with some costs a stamp per referenced project per poll.
- `docs/multi-project-api.md`: the tasks route's ETag; drop the note T-549 added that another project's change shows only once this one changes.

## Tests
The CLI suite (`serve.test.mjs`): A references B; a conditional GET of A's tasks after B's task changes is a **200** with the new values; after a change in an unrelated project C, still a **304**; with nothing changed, a 304; a new reference added to A then B changing: a 200. e2e (`keys.spec.ts`, the real binary's views): the browser's poll (`page.clock`) shows the other project's task done.

notes.text: The tasks route’s ETag (and the overview’s) also covers the task data of the projects named in `dependencies`, `related`, `duplicate_of` (archive too; `foreign::named_by`, worked out once per stamp of the project’s own data). A poll sees a named project’s change; an unrelated change stays a 304 (serve.test.mjs). No e2e: the fixture server has no ETags of atm’s

tasks.name: Store::subscribe in atm-db: how a store hears of changes is the store's; the app's file watcher moves behind it
tasks.description:
[The freshness design](docs/cross-project-freshness-design.md) §3 and §5.5, option **L** (P6): watching for changes is the store's job, behind the abstraction, so a store that isn't files (a `JiraStore`) works the same.

## Change
- **atm-db's `Store` trait:** `subscribe(on_change) -> Subscription` (dropping it ends it), replacing `watch_folders()`. Its documentation says `on_change` runs on the store's own thread, and that every store must push or poll.
- **`JsonGitStore`:** watches its own folders (the task folder, the claims store, the working copies' task files) with `notify` and its debouncer, settled 300 ms, the code now in the app (`app/src-tauri/src/commands.rs`, `AppState::watch`). `notify` and `notify-debouncer-full` move from the app to atm-db (same versions, already approved; no new dependency).
- **`MemoryStore`:** told by its own writes.
- **`poll_stamp(store, interval, on_change)`** in atm-db: a helper an implementation may use when it can't push (none needs it yet: test it on its own). No polling default in the trait (Hakan, round 1).
- **The registry** (`workspaces/<w>.json`): a subscription for "the list changed".
- **atm-lib:** a workspace's changes are its members' subscriptions merged, plus the registry's; the app's `subscribe_workspace` and `subscribe_project` use that. Nothing above atm-db names a folder to watch.
- Behaviour unchanged for the user: the app is told of the same changes as now (the open workspace's own projects); the browser polls.
- `docs/layered-architecture.md` and `docs/guides/tauri.md` (Streams) say where watching lives.

## Tests
atm-db: the JSON store's subscription tells a change in its task file and its claims and stops when dropped; `poll_stamp` tells a stamp change; the memory store tells its writes. atm-lib: a workspace subscription merges its members' and the registry's. The app's existing subscription tests (`a_subscription_says_when_a_watched_folder_changes…`, `a_window_loading_again…`) pass unchanged.

notes.text: `Store::subscribe(on_change)` in atm-db replaces `watch_folders`: the JSON store watches its own folders (notify, moved from the app), the memory store tells its writes, `poll_stamp` for stores that poll; the registry subscribes to the workspaces folder; atm-lib merges them (`Workspace::subscribe`, `Member::subscribe`). The app’s messages are the same; a burst touching two projects may now send two

tasks.name: The CLI: task text can't drive the terminal (control characters and escape sequences dropped)
tasks.description:
Found in 0.38.0's security review of T-488's styled output: task text (a name, a note, a description, anyone's who can change `tasks.json`) reached the terminal as written, so an escape sequence in it could set the clipboard (OSC 52), the window title or a link, clear the screen or hide text, and a carriage return could print over a line.

## Change
- `output::clean` in `crates/atm-cli/src/output.rs`: drops every control character but the line end and the tab; with styling on, keeps SGR sequences of atm's own styles only.
- The crate's own `println!`, `print!`, `eprintln!` and `eprint!` (in `main.rs`) shadow std's, so everything printed for people goes through it; `--json` prints exactly.
- [security-architecture.md](docs/security-architecture.md): invariant I30, and the review entry.

## Tests
`tests/scripts/output.test.mjs` "task text can’t drive the terminal".

notes.text: output::clean drops task text’s control characters before the terminal (I30); --json exact. Found in 0.38.0’s security review of T-488; the CLI suite (647) passes.
