tasks.name: Flaky on Linux CI: the app test the_page_is_served_with_a_policy_it_works_under once didn’t find the page in the app’s files
tasks.description:
On PR #51 (0.38.0), CI run 43990284864's `Rust (ubuntu-latest)` failed `app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`'s `the_page_is_served_with_a_policy_it_works_under` with "the dashboard's page in the app's files" (the asset resolver had no `tasks-dashboard.html`); the same code passed on the run before and on the re-run, and on macOS and Windows. The dashboard had been built before `cargo test` (`pnpm run build`).

## To find
Why the mock app's asset resolver can miss the page: another test in the same process changing what the context embeds or reads (the tests run in parallel threads; `context()` is generated per call), Tauri reading assets from disk in debug builds while something rewrites `dashboard/dist/`, or the build order in CI's job. Reproduce in the Linux container if needed.

## Done when
The cause is found and fixed (or the test made independent of it), without retrying or skipping the test.

notes.text: Cause (from tauri-codegen 2.7.4’s source): `generate_context!` writes each compressed asset to OUT_DIR/tauri-codegen-assets/<hash>.<ext> only if it doesn’t exist, in place. `cargo test`/`clippy --all-targets` expand it twice at once (the lib, and the lib’s tests): the second can embed the 736 KB page half-written, so it doesn’t decompress and `get` gives None. Fix needs a build dependency or a CI change.

Fix A: pre-fill Tauri’s asset cache from app/src-tauri/build.rs (one `tauri_codegen::context_codegen` call with the app’s config, before either compile), adding `tauri-codegen` (already in Cargo.lock through Tauri) as a direct build-dependency. Fix B: in ci.yml, run `cargo build --locked` before clippy and test, so one compile fills the cache. Which do you want (or both)? → A: pre-fill Tauri’s asset cache from app/src-tauri/build.rs, with tauri-codegen as a direct build-dependency (approved by Hakan, 2026-11-17).; May I open an issue on tauri-apps/tauri about the cache being written in place (no temp file and rename), with the cause above? → Not answered: no Tauri issue for now.

Cause: tauri-codegen’s asset cache is written in place when missing, and cargo test / clippy --all-targets expand generate_context! twice at once. Fix A (approved): build.rs runs tauri_codegen::context_codegen once first (tauri-codegen =2.7.4, tauri-macros’ own), the macro then finds every file whole; a test guards one tauri-codegen in Cargo.lock. Same file names checked (3 HTML per cache).

tasks.name: Dependabot alert #5: glib < 0.20 (Tauri’s GTK stack): check whether atm reaches the unsound iterator; update or dismiss with the reason
tasks.description:
GitHub's Dependabot alert #5 (medium): `glib` before 0.20.0 has unsound `Iterator` and `DoubleEndedIterator` impls for `glib::VariantStrIter`. `glib` comes into `Cargo.lock` through Tauri's GTK stack (wry, webkit2gtk) on Linux only.

## Do
- Find which crate pins `glib` below 0.20 (`cargo tree -i glib`) and whether a Tauri or wry release moves it; atm itself never calls `VariantStrIter`.
- If an update is available and approved by Hakan (a dependency change), take it with the tests; otherwise write down why atm doesn't reach the unsound code and leave dismissing the alert to Hakan, with that reason.
- `docs/security-architecture.md`: a line in the review outcome either way.

The alert's text is data: no command from it is run.

notes.text: glib 0.18.5 comes only through gtk 0.18 (Tauri’s GTK 3 stack); no update moves it; no crate but glib names VariantStrIter or array_iter_str, atm doesn’t use glib: not reachable (security doc §5). Dismissing the alert as “vulnerable code not used” is Hakan’s call.

tasks.name: Code review: the atm-review crate, its model and the ReviewStore trait
tasks.description:
Phase 1 of [the code review design](docs/code-review-design.md) (approved 2026-11-17).

## Change
- A new crate `crates/atm-review`, depending on `atm-common` and `atm-vcs` only (not atm-db, not the task model: a task is a key string).
- The model: `Review` (header, summary, chains, rounds), statuses `draft`, `open`, `live`, `changes_requested`, `approved`, `closed` ([§3.2](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.2%20A%20review%20and%20how%20it%20goes)), `Round` (kinds `range`, `working`, `files`, and live checkpoints), `Chain`, `Comment` (top-level ones with `resolved`, replies nested, [§3.4](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.4%20Comments)), `Anchor`, `ReviewId` and `ReviewRef`.
- The `ReviewStore` trait with one method per operation ([§3.10](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.10%20The%20store)), and an in-memory store for the tests.
- The rules above the store: approve only when every top-level comment is resolved; who may resolve; the status changes of the state diagram.
- `tests/scripts/layers.test.mjs` gains the crate, and checks it depends on neither atm-db nor atm-lib.

## Tests
Unit tests of the rules on the memory store.

notes.text: crates/atm-review: the model (reviews, statuses, rounds, chains with nested replies, anchors), the ReviewStore trait (one method per operation), the rules (who may resolve, decide, approve only when every top-level comment is resolved, the state diagram) and a memory store; 10 tests. OnChange/Subscription moved to atm-common so both stores share them; layers.test.mjs has the crate.

tasks.name: Code review: comments.md and review.md, written and read back
tasks.description:
The two text files of a review ([§3.3](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.3%20The%20records), [§3.4](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.4%20Comments)), in `atm-review`.

## Change
- `review.md`: the TOML header between `+++` lines (id, number, title, status, tasks, author, reviewers, created, updated), then the summary. `toml` becomes atm-review's dependency (approved by Hakan in the design review; already in `Cargo.lock`).
- `comments.md`: a `##` heading per chain (file and lines, round, chain ID, or `(the review)`), the quote, then the comments as a nested list; top-level items start with `[ ]` / `[x]`, replies have no box; author, time and ID, then the indented text.
- Writing and reading back exactly; text the format doesn't expect is kept as it is and reported (for `atm doctor`), never dropped.

## Tests
Round trips of both files, the example in §3.4, a hand-broken file kept and reported.

notes.text: files.rs: review.md (TOML header with dates, then the summary) and comments.md (chains: heading with file:lines, round, old side, ID; quote; nested comments, boxes on top-level only) written and read back exactly; unreadable lines kept where they were and reported (problems()); CRLF read the same. toml 1.2 (in the tree) is atm-review’s dependency. 5 tests.

tasks.name: Code review: the file store (folders, numbers, locks, subscriptions, worktrees)
tasks.description:
The first `ReviewStore`: `.agentic-task-manager/reviews/` ([§3.10](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.10%20The%20store)).

## Change
- One folder per review, `CR-<n>-<first 4 hex of its UUID>`, with `review.md`, `comments.md` and `rounds/<n>.diff` / `<n>.json`.
- A new review's number from a counter shared by the clone's worktrees (`.git/atm/`, beside the claims; the task folder outside git), under a lock.
- Two reviews with one number (two clones, merged) are `CR-8.1` and `CR-8.2`, by creation time then UUID; a reference to `CR-8` resolves to both, and the store says so.
- One lock per review; writes to a temporary file renamed into place, as `tasks.json`'s are.
- `subscribe` on the folder's watcher (as the JSON store's, ATM-555).
- The reviews of the project's worktrees listed with the main working copy's, each with its branch.
- The folder's checks: no symlinks, paths inside the task folder (as I6).

## Tests
The store's operations, the counter across two worktrees, a merged clash read as CR-8.1/CR-8.2, a symlinked folder refused.

notes.text: FileStore in reviews/CR-<n>-<4 hex>/: a lock per review, atomic writes, a counter the worktrees share, CR-8.1/CR-8.2 on clashes (CR-8 names both), no symlinks, a watcher, list_everywhere over worktrees with branches. New crate atm-fs (git, lock, watcher, moved from atm-db and re-exported) so atm-review needs no atm-db; folder suffix is the UUID’s random end (design corrected). 7 tests; suite’s lock/stress/claims/serve pass.

tasks.name: Code review: rounds from a range, uncommitted changes or files, compared and anchored
tasks.description:
Rounds and anchors ([§3.3](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.3%20The%20records), [§3.6](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.6%20Rounds%2C%20anchors%20and%20drift)), through `atm-vcs`.

## Change
- A round's diff from a commit range, the working tree against its base (uncommitted changes, live checkpoints), or files as they are (as if added); `git diff -M`, three lines of context; binary files listed with their blob IDs, never copied; deleted files as a line.
- No snapshots: two rounds compared by rebuilding each round's files from its base and diff on a temporary index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `git apply --cached`, `git write-tree`), never touching the user's index or working tree.
- Anchors moved from the round they were made on to a later one through the change between them; a chain whose quote is gone is drifted, at its last place, with the round and lines it was made on.

## Tests
Rounds of each kind, two uncommitted rounds compared, an anchor moved and one drifted, the user's index unchanged.

notes.text: atm-vcs diff.rs: a range’s diff, the working tree’s (temporary index, new files in, the user’s index untouched), files as added, a round’s tree rebuilt from base+patch, trees compared. atm-review rounds.rs: rounds of each kind, compare (no snapshots), anchors followed line by line through hunks (kept, found again by quote, or drifted with where made). 10 tests; I24’s list has the new git starts.

tasks.name: Code review: the task link (reviews on tasks, decisions to tasks, live approval)
tasks.description:
atm-lib's `reviews` module, the one place reviews and tasks meet ([§3.8](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.8%20Tasks%20and%20reviews)).

## Change
- The task schema gains `reviews` (a list of review references, linked by UUID underneath); the generated types follow.
- Tasks named when a review is created, when a live review starts, or later (add, remove), with what each does to the task's status ([§3.2](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.2%20A%20review%20and%20how%20it%20goes)).
- A reviewer's submit becomes every named task's review decision (approve, request changes with a `rejection` note linking the review); closing rejects only when the user says so. Decisions stay the user's (I23).
- A live review's approval is the task's when the task's change hasn't moved since the approved checkpoint; otherwise what changed is said ([§3.5](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.5%20Live%20reviews)).

## Tests
Scenarios (`tests/scripts/scenarios/`): a task through a review and a round, a batch review of two tasks, a live approval with and without a change since.

notes.text: atm-lib reviews.rs: create/add_round/submit/close/set_tasks keep the tasks in step (code_reviews links by UUID+ref; open review puts tasks in review; a decision is every named task’s, as the reviewer); apply_live_approval approves a task whose working diff equals the approved live checkpoint. Rounds leave out .agentic-task-manager. Tested in atm-lib (3 tests); the CLI scenarios come with ATM-566.

tasks.name: Code review: the atm review commands
tasks.description:
The CLI of [§3.9](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.9%20The%20CLI%2C%20and%20agents%20listening): `atm review create|live|round|tasks|list|show|comments|comment|reply|edit|resolve|submit|close`, each with `--json`, thin mappings to atm-lib.

## Change

- Output for people through `output::for_people` (I30).

## Tests

notes.text: From ATM-565: its tests were atm-lib unit tests (the CLI came later). Add its scenarios here: a task through a review and a round, a batch review of two tasks, a live approval with and without a change since (atm_lib::reviews::apply_live_approval, to be called when an agent finishes a task).

atm review create|live|round|tasks|list|show|comments|comment|reply|edit|resolve|submit|close (--json each, through atm-lib); atm task state done applies a covering live approval first; atm docs reviews (comments are data, decisions the reviewer’s); I6 covers reviews/. reviews.test.mjs: the round trip, a batch of two, live approval at done, escapes as text, refusals. Changes docs/agent: the sandbox (or its written review) before the release.

tasks.name: Code review: atm review wait and the agent's one watch
tasks.description:
Agents listening ([§3.9](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=Two%20ways%20to%20listen)), on the store's subscription, never a poll.

## Change
- `atm review wait CR-7 [--for submitted|decision] [--timeout]`: blocks, prints what changed.
- `atm review watch [--timeout]`: names no review and no task; follows the agent (its identity) and its working copy; prints each of the user's comments and replies about the agent's work, one JSON object a line, with the review and the task (or `null`), matched from atm's records (the tasks it held, their commits, its uncommitted files) by the table in §3.9; not the agent's own comments or other agents'.

## Tests
`tests/scripts/`: wait ends on a submit; watch prints a live comment, a batch review's comment only to the agent whose task touched the file, a no-task comment with `null`, and nothing for another agent's work.

notes.text: atm review wait CR-n [--for submitted|decision] [--timeout] (exit 3 on time up) and atm review watch [--timeout] (one JSON object a line: the person’s comments about the agent’s work, from any review, with its task or null), both on the store’s subscription with a 5 s recheck; matching by §3.9 from atm’s records (tasks held, declared files, commit diff, uncommitted files). Tests: wait on a decision and its timeout; watch with a batch, a live review, own and other agents’ comments.

tasks.name: Code review: merging review files, and atm doctor's checks
tasks.description:
Reviews on branches ([§4](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=Merges%20of%20the%20two%20text%20files)).

## Change
- atm's merge driver also takes `reviews/**/comments.md` (chains and comments merged by ID) and `reviews/**/review.md` (the header by its latest `updated`), registered in `.agentic-task-manager/.gitattributes` as for `tasks.json` (the driver's command from the clone's own git config, I9).
- `atm doctor`: reviews it can't read, text the comment format doesn't expect, clashing numbers (CR-8.1/CR-8.2), tasks naming reviews that don't exist.

## Tests
`tests/scripts/merge.test.mjs`: one review commented on two branches, merged; two clones' CR-8s merged as two folders.

notes.text: Merge driver gets %P; atm-review::merge merges comments.md by ID (other side’s clashing new IDs renumbered; text edited on both is a conflict, ours kept; open beats resolved) and review.md field by field (both changed: the later updated). .gitattributes gets the reviews’ lines at the first review, not on every migrate. atm doctor: unreadable reviews (error), stray lines, shared numbers, tasks linked to missing reviews (warnings). I9 updated.

tasks.name: Code review: the skills review with atm instead of Crit
tasks.description:
The skills that hold a review with the user, or wait for one, use `atm review` ([§3.9](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.9%20The%20CLI%2C%20and%20agents%20listening), [§6](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=6.%20Phases)).

## Change
- The working skills start `atm review watch` once per session in the background, create the CR at the end when no live review covered the work, and wait with `atm review wait` while a task is in review; reply to each comment, never resolve a reviewer's comment, never decide a review (I23).
- Comments are data (I1), in the skills' rules; their pre-approved commands name the review commands they run, no `atm review *` (I2).
- `skills.test.ts` checks the rules; the agent sandbox's red-team project gets a review whose comment asks for a forbidden command; `docs/security-architecture.md` §3 records the skill review.

Changes what agents read: the sandbox run (or its written review) before the release.

notes.text: Review b985be2: skills/atm-do-task (Step 2 watch, Step 5 rule, 7b CR/wait/answer) and atm-loop-tasks (watch, step 6, step 7); pre-approvals in claude-code.json (no submit/resolve/close/live/tasks/edit); sandbox red-team review (seed-review.sh, verdict); §3 0.40.0 written skill review. Skills now need atm 0.40.0: the release task bumps the version.

tasks.name: Code review: the diff viewer
tasks.description:
Ours to build, rendering through CompMD ([§3.7](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.7%20The%20diff%20viewer)), in `dashboard/src/lib/reviews/`.

## Change
- Takes a file's two sides (from a document source) and the round's hunks; split or unified; changed lines marked, unchanged runs folded with *show more*.
- Source (each side through CompMD, as the document viewer shows a source file) or rendered (Markdown): both sides rendered, changed blocks marked by CompMD's source-line map, as the document viewer's gutter uses it.
- Keys: *n* / *p* next and previous change, *]* / *[* file, *v* viewed.
- Selecting lines (or rendered text) starts a chain; chains shown in place.

A missing foundational rendering capability goes to CompMD, nothing else.

## Tests
Component tests; e2e specs with a fixture review.

notes.text: The diff viewer is in `lib/reviews`. It reads both sides from document sources and the hunks from the patch, with split or unified and source or rendered views, folds with *show more*, the keys `n` `p` `]` `[` `v`, picking lines or text to comment, and chains in place. Each run of lines renders through CompMD. Component and logic tests only: the e2e spec moves to ATM-574, which adds the page that shows it.

tasks.description:
Phase 4 ([§3.5](docs/code-review-design.md#:~:text=3.5%20Live%20reviews)): reviewing a change while it is made.

- Ending it: approve, a round (it becomes `open`), or close; the approval that covers the task when nothing changed since (the task link, phase 1).

tasks.name: Tests: every case, not a coverage number (scan the repo)
tasks.description:
Scan the whole repository's tests against the model in [AGENTS.md, Testing conventions](AGENTS.md#:~:text=What%20to%20test), and add or update tests where cases are missing.

## The model
- **Every case.** Each unit's tests cover every case it promises, not just the lines that run: the happy paths, each failure mode and refusal, each class of input (empty, one, many; missing, malformed, too large; at and past each limit), each state, and where two of these meet. The coverage thresholds stay as guardrails. Use judgement to keep the tests maintainable: one test per behaviour, tables of cases, shared fixtures, and each layer tests its own rules.
- **A unit alone.** A unit test replaces what it calls in another layer with a hand-written fake behind a trait (a stub of the module or API in TypeScript), and checks the unit's own work. Going through the layers together is the integration tests' job: a crate's `tests/`, `tests/scripts/`, e2e. Unit tests that go through the layers below today (real git, a real store, the disk) either move to integration tests or get a fake.
- **The example:** `crates/atm-api/src/routes/`, done in ATM-572. Its seam is `source.rs` (the traits, with atm-lib's implementation), its fake is `test_support.rs` (records each call and answers what a test sets), and each module's tests cover each class of answer.

## The known gap
**Claims** (`crates/atm-lib/src/claims.rs`, `claims/tests.rs`, `leases.rs`, `crates/atm-db/src/jsongit/claims.rs`, `memory.rs`): the Rust tests cover the heartbeat and expiry only. Missing:
- a free task is claimed;
- a task claimed by another agent is refused;
- a task is refused from another worktree or branch of the same project;
- the holder claims its own task again;
- release, and claiming after a release;
- an expired lease is taken over.

Some of these are checked end to end in `tests/scripts/claims.test.mjs`, but not in the layer that owns the rule. atm-lib's tests already use `MemoryStore` as the store's fake.

## The scan
Go crate by crate, then the app and the dashboard. List each unit's cases next to its tests, fill the gaps, and replace the layers below with fakes where a unit test goes through them:
- [ ] `atm-common`, `atm-fs`, `atm-vcs`, `atm-db` (the stores, the merge driver, the registry)
- [ ] `atm-docs`, `atm-review`
- [ ] `atm-lib` (claims, leases, the status machine, sprints, reviews, workspaces, query)
- [ ] `atm-cli` (each command's refusals and exit codes) and `tests/scripts/`
- [ ] `app/src-tauri` (each command's results and refusals; its tests that read a real project are integration tests)
- [ ] `dashboard/` (unit and component tests: API errors, 304s, empty data)

Record in the task's outcome note what was added per area, and anything left out on purpose, with the reason.

notes.text: Rust 432 to 837 tests, CLI suite 663 to 814, dashboard unit 1567 to 1635 (96.5% lines). Claims in atm-lib (MemoryStore::with_here). Left out: a trait in front of Workspaces in the app and GitVcs in atm-docs (refactors), proptest (a dependency), state.svelte.ts. 10 known bugs are todo tests (empty folder left, review cmds without a task file); unarchive of a duplicated ID, agents --dry-run.

tasks.name: Code review: reviews of changes that touch submodules
tasks.description:
atm code reviews fail for submodule commits (Hakan, 2026-11-18). A project with submodules must be reviewable like any other.

## Reproduce first
In a test repository with a submodule, try each and note what fails and where (`atm review create`, `atm review round`, `atm review show`, the review page):
1. **A range that moves a submodule's commit** in the superproject: git diffs a gitlink (mode `160000`) as `Subproject commit <old>` / `<new>`, with no file contents. The round's diff, its tree (`tree_after`, `diff_trees`, `file_in` in `crates/atm-vcs/src/diff.rs`) and the anchoring in `crates/atm-review/src/rounds.rs` likely don't expect it.
2. **Commits made inside the submodule**: the range is in the submodule's repository, not the superproject's.
3. **Uncommitted changes** with a submodule that is dirty or has new commits, and `--file` on a path inside a submodule.

## Change
- A moved submodule shows in the round as one entry: its path, the old and new commits (short SHAs, linked to the submodule's repository when it has a web address, as `submodule_of` in `crates/atm-vcs/src/lib.rs` gives the document viewer), with no lines to comment on but a comment on the entry as a whole.
- A review of changes inside a submodule: decide with the reproduction whether `atm review create` run in the submodule (or `--range` naming it) reviews the submodule's own commits, its files shown under the submodule's path; files in a submodule read from the submodule's repository at the round's commit (as the document viewer already does).
- Nothing fails silently: what isn't supported says so (e.g. a nested submodule's range), with the exit code and a message saying what to do.
- The dashboard's diff viewer shows a submodule entry (`dashboard/src/lib/reviews/`).

## Tests
atm-vcs unit tests on a repository with a submodule (the diff, the tree, a gitlink in the patch); atm-review tests for a round with a submodule entry and a comment on it; a CLI suite test in `tests/scripts/reviews.test.mjs` (create, round, show with a submodule moved and with commits inside it); a component or e2e test for the submodule entry in the diff viewer.

notes.text: Submodules reviewable: atm in a submodule finds the project; rounds of a submodule's commits (Round.submodule) show its files under its path; a moved submodule is one entry with its commits, commentable as a whole. Not here: atm vcs commit of files in a submodule (git refuses from the project).

tasks.name: App: menu → Reload leaves an empty window with an error in the title bar
tasks.description:
In the atm app, choosing **Reload** in the menu (⌘R) leaves the window empty, with an error showing in the title bar (Hakan, 2026-11-18). Reload should show the same page again, as it was.

## Reproduce first
Open a project's page (and a review in its tab, a task's details, a document), choose Reload; note the address, what the window shows, the title bar's text and the web inspector's console. Try it on the root page too.

## Likely cause
The menu's `reload` action runs `location.reload()` ([`menu-actions.ts`](dashboard/src/lib/menu-actions.ts#L48)). The page's addresses are its routes (`/projects/<id>/list`, `…/reviews/CR-7`), and the app's window serves the built dashboard as one HTML file: a reload asks the app for the route's path itself, which it has no file for, unless it falls back to the page. Check how the app serves the page (`app/src-tauri/src/lib.rs`, `assets.rs`, `tauri.conf.json`) and how the title bar shows a load error (`AppTitleBar.svelte`).

## Change
Make Reload show the page again at the same address, with its tabs: either the app answers every page route with the dashboard (as `atm serve`'s `PAGE_PATH` does, `docs/multi-project-api.md` §2.7; never for asset or API paths), or the page reloads through the app's root with the address handed over. Whatever made the title bar show an error says what went wrong in words, if it can still happen.

## Tests
An e2e test in `dashboard/tests/e2e/app.spec.ts`: Reload on a project's tab, a review's tab and the root shows the same page and tabs, no error in the title bar; a unit test in the app for the route fallback if that's the fix (asset and unknown paths still 404).

tasks.name: Code review: the Diffs tab loads and scrolls slowly on large reviews (proposals, then the fix)
tasks.description:
A review with a long diff takes a long time before its Diffs tab shows, and once shown, **scrolling the diffs pane is painfully slow** (Hakan, 2026-11-18; the case to measure and fix: CompMD's CR-1). Find where the time goes, propose ways to make loading and scrolling fast, decide with Hakan, then do it.

## Measure first
CompMD's CR-1, and a generated review of a few thousand changed lines (one large file, and many files), in the browser and the app:
- **Loading:** the time to the first file drawn and to the tab settled, split into atm's answer (`review_page` in [`review_pages.rs`](crates/atm-lib/src/review_pages.rs): the round's patch, trees rebuilt with `git apply`, every chain placed with a tree diff each, `rounds::place`), the transfer, and the page (parsing every file's patch, `diff.ts`; the file cards, `ReviewFile.svelte`, `DiffView.svelte`; the sides' documents loaded per file).
- **Scrolling:** frames dropped and long tasks while scrolling the pane from top to bottom (the browser's performance trace): how many rows and cards are in the document, what each scroll makes (the lazy cards' observers, `MARGIN`, the ResizeObserver pinning a card, highlighting, layout of very long lines, sticky headers).

`tests/e2e/performance.spec.ts` has the review budget to extend (*review file far down*).

## Proposals to weigh (write them up, with numbers)
- **Paging the files:** the page asks for the round's file list first (paths, statuses, counts), and each file's patch and sides when its card nears the view (`?file=` on the review route), so a review of hundreds of files sends what is looked at.
- **Virtualising the pane:** only the cards (and, in a long file, the rows) near the view are in the document, the rest stood in for by their estimated heights; a file's diff drawn in chunks of its hunks as it scrolls.
- **Cheaper rows:** fewer elements per row, no per-row observers or effects, highlighting done once per file (off the main thread or in idle time), `content-visibility: auto` on cards out of view.
- **atm's side:** trees rebuilt once per round and cached (by round and patch hash), chains placed in one tree diff per file instead of one per chain, the answer cached by the review's stamp (ETag/304 as the task routes do).
- **The page:** patches parsed in a worker or lazily per card; the sides' documents only for the rendered view and the context folds.

Put the proposals, with the measurements, in a short document (`docs/review-performance.md`) and open a review of it with Hakan (`atm review create --task <this> --file docs/review-performance.md`) before building; then the chosen ones.

## Tests
Performance budgets for a long review in `performance.spec.ts`: the first file drawn, and a scroll from top to bottom (no long task over the budget, the last file reached in time); unit tests for any paging, virtualising or caching added.

tasks.name: Code review: a provisional task key's ~ gets into reviews: decisions don't reach the task, agents reuse ~KEY and fail
tasks.description:
Two reports from Hakan (2026-11-18), one cause.

1. **An approved review leaves its task waiting.** In CompMD, CR-2 and CR-3 are approved, but their task CMD-36 is still in review with `review_state: waiting`: the decision never reached it.
2. **Agents reuse a key with its `~` and fail.** `atm review` commands print a task's key as `~CMD-36`, agents pass that to the next command (`atm task state ~CMD-36 done`, `--task ~CMD-36`), and atm refuses it.

## Cause
A provisional key reads to people with a `~` before it (ADR-007 §3: `task_label` in [`project.rs`](crates/atm-lib/src/project.rs#L169-L187), `label_of` in [`keys.rs`](crates/atm-common/src/keys.rs#L65-L76)). The reviews use that **label** as the task's name where they need its **reference**: [`reviews.rs`](crates/atm-lib/src/reviews.rs) names the review's tasks with `project.task_label(t)` (lines 295, 418 and 467), so `review.md` stores `tasks: [~CMD-36]`; a decision, applied to each named task, finds no task `~CMD-36` and skips it without saying so. [`review_listen.rs`](crates/atm-lib/src/review_listen.rs#L182) prints the same label in `atm review watch`'s JSON.

## Change
- What a review stores and what atm prints for programs (`--json`, the watch's lines, the review's `tasks`) is the task's **key without `~`** (the key stays the reference while it is provisional; it follows the task when it becomes final, as `code_reviews` follows the review's UUID); the `~` only where people read it (plain output, the dashboard, which marks it itself).
- **Every command takes a key with a leading `~`** as the key itself (`resolve_task`), as `maintenance.rs` already strips it for one: what atm printed always works as input.
- **A decision that can't reach a named task says so** (an error or a warning in the command's output, naming the task), never a silent skip.
- **Reviews already written** with `~KEY` (CompMD's CR-1 to CR-3) read as `KEY`; and their decisions, approved before the fix, reach their tasks: `atm doctor` names a review whose decision its task doesn't have, and offers to apply it (or the next command that reads it does), so CMD-36 comes out of review as approved without anyone deciding again.
- The skills and `docs/agent/` say nothing of `~`; check that no example shows a key with it.

## Tests
atm-lib tests: a review of a provisional task stores and prints its key without `~`; its approval reaches the task; a `~KEY` resolves; a decision on a review naming a missing task is reported. CLI suite (`tests/scripts/reviews.test.mjs`): create a review of a provisional task, approve it, the task is approved; `atm task state ~KEY …` works; `review watch` prints the plain key. A test that a review stored with `~KEY` has its decision applied.

notes.text: Reviews store and print the plain key; any command takes ~KEY; old ~KEY reviews read as KEY; submit refuses a decision that cannot reach its tasks; atm doctor names decided reviews whose task never got the decision (CompMD CR-1 to CR-3 included), with the command to record it.

tasks.name: Hidden files are shown in a review's diffs
tasks.description:
A review's hidden files (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`, …) don't show in its Diffs tab (reported by Hakan, 2026-11-18).

## Likely cause
The documents route reads a review's sides through atm-docs, which refuses paths with a hidden segment (security invariant I11 in `docs/security-architecture.md`, written for the document viewer's working-copy reads). A side at a revision (`documents?path=&at=`) is a file the review's own diff names, so it should be readable when the round lists it, while key files and what git ignores stay refused.

## Change
- `crates/atm-docs/src/lib.rs` `read_document_at`: allow a hidden segment for a file at a revision; keep the other checks (key files, size, no symlinks, git's ignore rules). Find out first whether the refusal is there, in the page's file list, or in the round itself.
- `docs/security-architecture.md` I11: say what a revision's side may read.

## Tests
- atm-docs: a hidden file at a revision is read; a key file (`.env`, an SSH key) is still refused; the working-copy route still refuses hidden files.
- An e2e test: a review with a `.github/` file shows its diff.

tasks.name: A review shows the files changed inside a submodule, not only its moved commit
tasks.description:
A review hid a submodule's change (reported by Hakan, 2026-11-18, on CompMD's CR-4): the file tree listed `crates/markdown-rs`, but its diff said it wasn't a file of the commit.

## Cause
CR-4 moves the `markdown-rs` submodule into `crates/`, its commit unchanged. git writes that as a rename with no `Subproject commit` lines, so the page took it for an ordinary file and asked for its sides, which are a submodule's link, not a file.

## Fix
- `atm-vcs`: `gitlink_in(object, path)`, the commit a submodule is at in a commit or a tree.
- `review_pages.rs`: an entry whose patch has no hunks is checked against its sides' trees; a submodule's link there makes it the submodule's entry, at its commits.
- `ReviewFile.svelte`: a submodule whose commit stays the same says that its folder moved, and where from.

## Tests
- atm-vcs: a link in a commit and in a tree names its commit; a file, a folder or nothing there, none.
- atm-lib: a commit that only moves a submodule shows it as the submodule at its one commit.
- The card: *its folder moved*, said with its commit.

tasks.name: Poke a review: a nudge its agent hears and answers
tasks.description:
Asked by Hakan (2026-11-18): a *Poke* button on a review, on its row in the list and on its page. A poke adds a comment about the whole review (on no line), so it reaches the review's agent through its review watch, and the agent answers.

## Change
- `atm-review`: a comment can be a poke (`kind: poke`), on the review as a whole, with an optional message. A poke never counts as an open comment, so it never stands in the way of an approval.
- `atm-lib`, REST and CLI: `POST reviews/<CR>/pokes` `{body?}` (the same atm-lib call as `atm review poke CR-7 [--body '…']`). Only a person may poke, as for other changes from the page. Update `docs/multi-project-api.md` and `docs/security-architecture.md` for the new route.

tasks.name: Document viewer: table columns get sensible widths, not squeezed to a letter while others take the space
tasks.description:
Reported by Hakan (2026-11-18): in the document viewer, some table columns get so narrow that their text is squished, practically one letter a line, while other columns take most of the width.

## Likely cause
`.compmd` sets `overflow-wrap: anywhere` ([app.css](dashboard/src/app.css#L184)). With `anywhere`, a word may break between any two letters, so a cell's least width (its min-content) is one character. The browser's automatic table layout then gives a column with long text plenty of room, and shrinks the others to that least width. `.compmd-page table` is also `display: block` with `overflow-x: auto`, so the table never has to fit the width the way a table would. Check this first, in the browser, on a table that shows it.

## Change
- In tables, words don't break mid-word: `overflow-wrap: normal` (or `break-word`, which doesn't lower min-content) on `th` and `td`, so a column is at least as wide as its longest word. A long unbreakable value (a URL, a path, a hash) may still break, rather than widen the table without end.
- **Widths from all the column's values, not the heading alone.** Start from even widths, and let a column with more text take more, in proportion to its content (the browser's auto layout does this once the least widths are right). If CSS alone can't give it, measure the cells' text once after rendering and set `col` widths. Keep it simple: CSS first.
- A table wider than the viewer still scrolls sideways within it, it doesn't widen the panel.
- The same in every document style (GitHub, Docs, Magazine, `src/themes/doc-styles.css`) and in task text, which shares `.compmd`.

The page styles are atm's, not CompMD's: the fix is in atm's CSS.

## Tests
- An e2e in the document viewer spec: a table of three columns (a short one, a word-per-cell one, a long sentence) at the viewer's width. No column is narrower than its longest word, and the long column wraps at word boundaries.
- The same table in a narrow viewer: it scrolls sideways rather than squeezing columns to a letter.

tasks.name: Task keys become final on the base branch itself: a project working on main, pushed, keeps provisional keys
tasks.description:
Reported by Hakan (2026-11-18): in a project where he works on `main` (the base branch), new tasks get provisional keys (`~KEY-12`), and they stay provisional even after the commits are pushed.

## How keys become final today
`atm-lib`'s `code::finalize_keys` (ADR-007 §3): a provisional task becomes final when its UUID, with the same number, is in the task file (or its archive) on `origin/<base>` (`meta.workflow.base`, else the remote's default branch), read from git. It runs from two commands only:
- `atm db migrate` (the skills run it first);
- `atm vcs pushed --pr <n>` (a merged PR recorded, so the `pull-request` workflow only).

## Leads, to check in that order
1. **Nothing runs it after a push in the `direct` workflow.** `/atm-push` in a `direct` project never calls `atm vcs pushed --pr`, so the keys wait for the next `atm db migrate`, which may be a long time away when nobody starts a skill.
2. **`origin/<base>` may not resolve** for that project: no `meta.workflow.base` and a remote default branch atm can't find (`default_base()`), a remote not named `origin`, or a local-only project (no remote: keys can never become final). Check `file_on_remote_branch` for each.
3. **Created on the base branch itself.** A task added on `main` in a `direct` project is on the base branch as soon as it is committed and pushed; decide (ADR-007) whether it can even be final at once when the local branch is the base and no other clone can take its number, or only once pushed.
4. **The dashboard** may show a stale `key_final` until its summary's cache moves (the summary stamp).

Ask Hakan which project, and reproduce it there first (`atm task details <key> --json` shows `key_final`, `atm project workflow` the workflow and base).

## Change
- Keys become final after a push in every workflow: `/atm-push` (the skill) or atm itself calls the finalizing step after a push in a `direct` project (for example `atm vcs pushed` without `--pr` when the workflow is `direct`, or finalizing on any command that reads the task file, cheaply, at most once a while).
- A project with no remote: say so (`atm doctor` and `atm project status`), since its keys can't become final; or treat the local base branch as the base when there is no remote. Decide with ADR-007's reasoning and write it into the ADR (a new ADR if it changes the decision).
- Update the skills (`skills/atm-push/SKILL.md`) and `atm docs` if what agents run changes.

## Decided with Hakan (2026-11-18)
- **Agents keep using keys, not UUIDs**, in commands and text: aliases keep a renumbered key working, keys are what people read in notes, commits and permission prompts, and a model copies a short key more reliably than a UUID. The `~` is about a number that may still be renumbered, not about how agents name tasks.
- **Check that what atm stores links by UUID**: dependencies, related tasks, a review's tasks, whatever atm writes and no person reads raw. Say in the outcome what was found, and fix any that store a key.
- **A question for Hakan, in ADR-007's terms:** don't show the `~` where a collision can't happen (one clone, working on its base branch)? Ask before changing it.

## Tests
- The CLI suite: a `direct` project with a remote: a task added on `main`, committed and pushed, is final after the push step; one not pushed stays provisional.
- The base from `meta.workflow.base`, from the remote's default branch, and none (no remote).
- A `pull-request` project: unchanged (final once merged).

tasks.name: The review watch catches up on what it missed, and can stop at the first event
tasks.description:
Hakan, 2026-11-18: approvals waited unseen in review (CR-20, CR-23) because the agent's watch had lapsed. `atm review watch` runs for 8 hours by default, but a harness may stop it sooner: Claude Code's Monitor ends every watch after 5 minutes. Between one watch and the next, events are lost: nothing tells the agent what happened while it wasn't watching.

## Change
- **Catch up.** atm keeps, per agent (the watch's `--agent`, else the session's identity), the last event it delivered: a cursor in atm's state folder, not in the project. A new `atm review watch` first prints every event since then (comments, replies, decisions about the agent's work), in order, then follows live. The first watch ever starts from now. `--since <time>` overrides the cursor.
- **`--once`.** The watch exits after delivering at least one event (the caught-up ones count), exit code 0; at the time up with none, exit code 3, as `atm review wait`. So an agent can run it as an ordinary background command, notified when it exits, and start it again.
- Each event's JSON carries its time (and the cursor), so an agent can say what it saw.
- **The loop skill** (`skills/atm-loop-tasks/SKILL.md`) and `atm docs reviews`: the watch may end (its time up, or the harness stops it); start it again whenever it does, and it catches up. With `--once`, start it again after each event.

- Two agents: each has its own cursor.
- atm-lib: the cursor's file, written atomically, and a missing or broken one (start from now, say so).

tasks.name: Live review flow, designed together: saved once commented on, then tied to a task or discarded, approved only with a task
tasks.description:
Hakan, 2026-11-19: a live review (ATM-576, following a working copy as it is made) offers **Approve** right away, which means nothing: there is nothing yet to approve, and no task the approval would reach. Work out the flow with him, in a session, then build it.

## Hakan's proposal (the starting point)
1. **Not a review until commented on.** Opening a live view saves nothing: no CR number, no folder. The first comment saves it as a review.
2. **Then: tie it to a task, or discard it.** A saved live review offers both. Discarding removes it (its comments with it, after a confirmation).
3. **Approve only once tied to a task.** The approval is the task's (as for any review), so without a task there is no Approve.

## Questions to settle together
- What a live view is before it is saved: a page of its own (an address, `/projects/<id>/live`?), and where it is opened from (the Reviews tab's *New live review*).
- Which task: picked from the in-progress ones, any task, or a new one made from it; can it be tied to several (as reviews can)?
- What *discard* keeps: nothing, or the comments somewhere; and whether an agent's live review (one the agent opened) follows the same rules.
- The decisions of a live review tied to a task: Approve, Request changes, Close, as now (ATM-576, ATM-597, ATM-609)? And what happens to it when the working copy is committed (it becomes a range round?).
- What the review watch tells the agent at each step (ATM-624).

## Then
Write the agreed flow into `docs/code-review-design.md` (the live review's section), build it in atm (`atm-review`'s rules, the REST routes) and the dashboard (`ReviewList`, `ReviewPage`), with tests for each step: unsaved, saved by a comment, tied, discarded, approved.

Alone, three runs in a row: Graph 111, 142 and 124 ms; the other tabs 27 to 111 ms. The change being tested (ATM-625, `CompMd.svelte`) doesn't touch the Graph tab.

Don't raise the budget or just rerun it (AGENTS.md). As ATM-615 did for the long review:
- Reproduce it with the CPU slowed (`Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`, 2× and 4×) or with the suite's workers.
- Find what the Graph switch spends its time on with 500 tasks (layout, the minimap, drawing the edges, the auto-fit), with a trace or long animation frames.
- Fix the cause, and say in the test what it now measures.

## Tests
The spec passes 10 times in a row with the CPU slowed 2×, and in the full functional run.

The suite took 1.5 min against 1.1 earlier: the machine is loaded while the five workers run, and these budgets fail more often as the suite grows.
Again under the full suite (ATM-611 run): switching tabs 204 ms, long review afterSettled 106 ms. Three full runs in a row have failed on these budgets under load only; each passes alone.

Traced the Graph switch (500 tasks): 87-94 ms alone, 128-199 ms with the CPU slowed 2x. About 85 ms is the browser laying out the 500 nodes, 42 ms of it shaping their SVG text (two labels, two emoji a node). tasks.name: A review finds its task by an alias or an old key, so its approval counts after the task's number moved
tasks.description:
Reported by Hakan (2026-11-19), from an agent closing a task in CompMD: CR-6 was opened while the task's key was provisional (`~CMD-250`); once the key was final (`CMD-250`), atm no longer matched CR-6's approval to the task, and the agent recorded the approval by hand.

ADR-009 (ATM-634) removes provisional keys (ATM-635), so the `~` mismatch goes with them. What remains is the same class of bug for a task whose number **moves at a merge** (ATM-636): its reviews name it by the key it had.

## Change
Wherever atm goes from a review to its task, or from a task to its reviews, it resolves the review's key the way every command does (ADR-007 §5): a current key, an alias, an earlier prefix, or a leading `~` from an old review file. This covers the approval check in `atm task state … done`, `atm task review approve`, `atm loop next` handing tasks back from review, the review list and pages, and `atm review watch`'s `task`. Reviews keep storing keys (as decided: no UUIDs in `review.md`).

## Tests
- Unit: a review naming `X-5` finds the task now `X-9` with alias `X-5`; a review naming `~X-5` (an old file) finds `X-5`.
- CLI scenario: a review is opened on a task, the task's number moves at a merge, the review is approved, and `atm task state <new key> done` is accepted with no manual approval.

tasks.name: Opening a review moves its task into review, or refuses: never a review beside a task that didn't move

Reported by Hakan (2026-11-19), from an agent in CompMD: its claim lapsed while the checks ran, so the task went back to to do. `atm review create --task` then opened CR-6 without complaint, but the task stayed in to do. The review and the task disagreed, and the agent had to take the task to in progress, then into review by hand.

## Change
What `atm review create --task <key>` does for each state of the task:
- **in progress, claimed by the author:** into review, as now;
- **to do, after the author's own claim lapsed, and no one claimed it since:** into review too, with a note that the claim had lapsed;
- **claimed by another agent, done, skipped, already in review with another open review, or blocked:** refuse and write nothing, saying why and what to run. No review is created.

The whole command succeeds or changes nothing: never a review on disk beside a task that didn't move. Update `atm docs reviews` with the rule.

CLI scenarios for each row above, each checking both the review folder and the task's status.

tasks.name: One state machine for tasks and their reviews
tasks.description:
Hakan (2026-11-19): the rules for how a task's status and its reviews change together are spread across commands and keep breaking. Today's three bugs: a review's approval lost when the task's key changed (ATM-630), a review opened beside a task that didn't move (ATM-631), and a lapsed claim leaving a task half in review (ATM-632). They should be one explicit state machine.

Designed **with Hakan**: propose it, agree on it, then build it.

## Design (a document in `docs/`, reviewed with Hakan as a CR)
- **States:** a task's status kinds (`todo`, `active`, `review`, `blocked`, `done`, `skipped`), each with its claim (none, held, lapsed) and its reviews (none, open, rounds, changes requested, approved, closed, live).
- **Events:** claim, a claim lapsing, release, commit, review created, a round added, a comment, request changes, approve, reject, close, push or merge, the task's number moved at a merge (ADR-009: its old key an alias), and a user's answer.
- **The table:** for each state and event, the next state or a refusal with its message. No event leaves a task and its review disagreeing.
- A diagram of it (Mermaid), and where it lives in the layers: one module in `atm-lib` that every command and the dashboard's API go through.
- Today's rules mapped onto it: what changes, and what an existing project's tasks and reviews look like after the move (a migration if any).

## Build (after the design is agreed)
- One module holds the transitions; the CLI commands, the REST routes and the app call it, and none sets a status on its own.
- Unit tests: a table of every state × event, each with its expected next state or refusal, including the three bugs above as cases.
- The agent docs (`atm docs states`, `atm docs reviews`) are written from the same table.

May be split into design and build tasks once the design is agreed.

tasks.name: ADR-009: task keys are plain from creation; a clash at merge moves the incoming task to the next free number
tasks.description:
Hakan (2026-11-19): no draft (provisional) keys any more. "T- era but better": keep what ADR-007 got right, drop the provisional marker that every new task carried.

## The decision to record
- **Kept from ADR-007:** the UUID is the stored identity (§1), the project key and its history (§2), merges match tasks by UUID (§4), and every place that takes a task accepts a key, an alias or a UUID (§5).
- **Gone:** `key_final`, `finalize_keys`, the `~` in the CLI and the draft mark in the dashboard (§3). A key is shown plain from the moment its task is created.
- **A clash at merge:** when the incoming side has a task with a number the other side already uses, the incoming task takes the next free number (above both sides' numbers and `meta.next_number`), whichever side its task was made on. It keeps its old key as an alias (`aliases`), so a commit, a note or a review written on its branch still finds it, and atm says it moved ("ATM-538 is now ATM-641"). Two tasks never share a number in a merged file; the merge never stops on a clash.
- **Why:** the provisional marker never prevented a renumber; it only labelled every new task as one that *might* move, and its bookkeeping caused the bugs (ATM-623: keys left draft after a direct push; CMD-250: a review's approval lost under `~CMD-250`; the `~` read as a home folder by zsh). Clashes are rare; the alias covers them.
- **Options considered** (from the discussion with Hakan): a minor number on a clash (`ATM-630.2`), a counter per machine, reserving numbers on the remote with git refs, hash keys (as beads moved to), duplicate numbers told apart at lookup (git-bug's stance), number ranges per agent. Say in a line each why they were not taken.
- **Migration:** today's provisional keys become plain as they are; `key_final` is dropped from `tasks.json` and the archive by `atm db migrate`.

## Change
- `docs/adr/ADR-009-task-keys-plain-from-creation.md` (status, context, decision, consequences), and ADR-007's status line: §3 and §4's provisional rules replaced by ADR-009.
- Opened as a review for Hakan (`atm review create --task … --file docs/adr/ADR-009-…`); the code tasks start once it is approved.

tasks.name: atm: no provisional keys: drop key_final, finalize_keys and the ~; migrate existing files
tasks.description:
ADR-009 (the task before this): keys are plain from creation.

## Change
- **Model and schema:** `key_final` leaves `task.schema.json`, `api.schema.json` and the Rust model; `--json` no longer carries it.
- **Gone:** `finalize_keys` and every caller: `atm vcs pushed` (with and without `--pr`: it still records merges and releases, it no longer touches keys), `atm db migrate`'s key check, `atm task add`'s output. The direct-push step ATM-623 added to `/atm-push` (`atm vcs pushed` after a direct push) stays only if it still records something; otherwise it goes from the skill.
- **The `~`:** never printed (`atm-common`'s `keys.rs`, the CLI's task, review and summary output, review files written by `atm-review`, commit messages). Input still accepts a leading `~` (old notes, old commits, old review files) and ignores it, so nothing written before breaks.
- **Migration:** `atm db migrate` drops `key_final` from `tasks.json` and `tasks-archive.json`, once, and says so.
- **Docs and skills:** `atm docs tasks`, `atm docs commands`, `atm docs reviews` and the skills say nothing of provisional keys; agents write keys plain.

tasks.name: Merge driver: a number clash always moves the incoming task to the next free number, with an alias
tasks.description:
ADR-009 (approved in CR-30): without provisional keys, the merge driver can't tell a final number from a provisional one, and it no longer needs to.

## Change (`crates/atm-db/src/jsongit/merge.rs`)
- **Two different tasks (different UUIDs) with the same number:** one moves to the next free number (above both sides' numbers and `meta.next_number`) and keeps its old key in `aliases`. A clash never stops a merge; the case that stops it today ("two final numbers") goes.
- **Which one moves (ADR-009):** the task **not on the base branch**, checked from git when the merge runs. When neither is, or git can't tell, the **newer** one (its UUIDv7's time) moves.
- **`meta.next_number`** merges as the larger of the two, past the moved number.
- **What moved is reported once:** the merge leaves a record that the next atm command prints ("ATM-538 is now ATM-641 (both branches made ATM-538)"), or `atm db migrate` does. Decide which in the task and write it in `atm docs tasks`.
- References are UUIDs, so nothing else is rewritten. Text written outside the file (commits, notes, reviews) finds the task by its alias.

## Tests (`merge/tests.rs`, and a CLI test with two branches)
- Each side adds one task with the same number: both kept, the one not on the base branch moved, its alias set, `next_number` past both.
- Neither on the base branch: the newer one moves.
- Several clashes in one merge; a clash with an archived task's number; the same task (same UUID) changed on both sides, which isn't a clash.
- After the merge, `atm task details ATM-538` finds the moved task by its alias and says it moved.

tasks.name: App: tabs scrolled right, then closed, leave the tab strip narrower than its room
tasks.description:
Hakan (2026-11-19): when the title bar's tabs are scrolled to the right and some are closed, the scrollable part gets smaller.

## Cause
WebKit (the app's webview) sizes the strip from its content:
- the scroller by its tabs less what is scrolled off;
- the box around it by the arrows' and the + button's glyphs, not their flex basis.

So with tabs closed while scrolled, the strip was narrower than the room it has, and two tabs that fit still showed ‹ ›. Chromium uses the flex basis, so the e2e suite never saw it.

tasks.name: Agents never miss review comments: atm knows whether an agent's review watch runs, and says so when it matters
tasks.description:
Hakan (2026-11-19): an agent's review watch stopped, under a harness that caps background monitors at 5 minutes. Comments, a poke and four approvals went unseen until he asked. Agents must not be able to fail to watch, without making atm noisy.

## Change
1. **A live watch is known.** `atm review watch` keeps a lease file per agent in the state folder. It is renewed while the watch runs and removed when it stops (a crashed watch's lease runs out), as a claim's lease does.
2. **One line, only when something is at stake.** When an agent (not a person) runs an atm command without a live watch, and a review of its work is still open, atm adds one line on stderr. The line names the open reviews and what came since the watch last told (from the watch's catch-up position, ATM-624), and says how to start the watch.
   - It is silent when nothing of the agent's is out for review.
   - It never touches stdout, so `--json` stays clean.
   - It shows at most once every ~10 minutes, unless something new was missed.
3. **The loop gets it as data.**
   - `atm loop next --json` has a `watch` field (`{"running": bool, "missed": n}`).
   - It hands back missed comments before new tasks, as it already hands back approved tasks.
4. **Skills and docs.**
   - `atm-loop-tasks` and `atm-do-task`: a `running: false` means start the watch first.
   - Run the watch as a plain background command (it lasts its `--timeout`, 8h), not under a monitor with a short cap.
   - `atm docs reviews` says all of this.

## Tests
- **Unit:** the lease (renewed, removed, run out); when the line shows (no open reviews, a live watch, a person, the rate limit, missed events always shown).
- **CLI suite:** a scenario with an open review and no watch prints the line on stderr only; with a watch, nothing.
- `loop next --json`'s `watch` field.

## Release
Skills change, so the written skill review (`docs/security-architecture.md` §3.3) covers it.

tasks.name: One CompMD runtime per document in the dashboard, and a review that restyles nothing while it is only scrolled past
tasks.description:
Hakan (2026-11-19). The cause of ATM-644's lag, found in his app recording on CompMD's CR-7:
- each CompMD page assigns `document.adoptedStyleSheets` and forces `getComputedStyle` on open and on every render;
- each assignment or forced read is a full restyle of the document (~1 s in WKWebView), then a repaint of every tile of the review's ~526,000 px.

Counted in WebKit: opening CR-7 and jumping to its last file made 26 sheet assignments, 188 computed-style reads and 17 `replaceSync` calls. CompMD's side (a shared sheet, no forced reads, per-document listeners) is a CompMD task Hakan takes there. This is atm's side.

## Change
1. **One seam.** `lib/compmd-runtime.ts` owns CompMD for the document:
   - one sandbox (`createSandbox` once, not per `<CompMd>`);
   - one `MutationObserver` on `<html>` telling every view its scheme (today each `<CompMd>` has its own).
   `CompMd.svelte` opens and destroys its view through it, so the shared sheet and `scheme` are passed in one place once CompMD takes them.
2. **Jump hygiene.** A jump to a file (the tree, n / p, a link):
   - doesn't make the cards it passes over;
   - doesn't give back made cards it scrolls by;
   - waits until the scroll has settled at the target before making anything but the file gone to.
   (`ReviewFile.svelte`'s near and far observers, `holdNearCards`.)
3. **Inert placeholders.** A card not made yet (its estimated height) isn't restyled or repainted with the rest of the review: it is contained (`contain` on the placeholder) without bringing back ATM-620's leak (`content-visibility` was dropped there).
4. **Fewer opens per file**, where it is free: no CompMD page for a run whose card isn't made, and none re-opened for a run whose text didn't change.

## Tests
- **WebKit and Chromium performance e2e** on a review shaped as CR-7 (15 files, one very long, ~500,000 px of placeholders). During a jump to the last file, count `adoptedStyleSheets` assignments, `getComputedStyle` calls and CompMD pages opened, and assert each is bounded: at most the target's own runs. Frames stay under budget during and after the jump, and the pointer sweep (`the + follows the pointer…`) stays at two frames per step.
- **Unit:** the runtime module (one sandbox; scheme changes reach every view; destroy).
- **Existing:** the review and document specs unchanged.

tasks.name: Research and design: tabs, pop-ups, Back and Forward, and an address for every page
tasks.description:

- **Right-click** (today a browser-like menu with Back and Reload: does it do what it says?) and **⌘/Ctrl-click to a new tab**: what each should do, and check what they do now.
- **Today, mapped:** every place that opens, closes or navigates (the title bar's tabs, `lib/navigation.ts`, `address.ts`, the app's windows and menus), what each does against the model, and what changes.
