tasks.name: atm loop next hands a task back from review (approved or changes requested) to its agent
tasks.description:
Audit finding L1 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#l1-high-bug-a-task-back-from-review-is-never-handed-out-by-atm-loop-next-checked)).

`Approve`, `RequestChanges` and `Reject` are in `WAITING_COMMANDS` (`crates/atm-lib/src/changes.rs:34`), so a decision, also one made on a code review (`reviews::submit`), writes a `waiting` record. `loop_order` (`crates/atm-lib/src/loop_rules.rs:314`) then skips every task with a `waiting` record from any worktree, so rework candidates never reach `ready`, and the reason says the task waits in another worktree.

## Change
- In `loop_order`, ignore `waiting` records whose `worktree` is this one, as `status.rs:208` does (pass `here` in).
- Stop recording `Approve` and `RequestChanges` as a wait, or clear the record when the task is handed back.
- `next_task_for` (`changes.rs:499-501`) inserts the claim but doesn't clear `completed` and `waiting` as `change_task_status`'s Start arm does: share one `record_start(work, here, task_id, agent)`.

Coordinate with ATM-633 (the state machine): if it already replaced this code, make this a test of it.

## Tests
- A scenario in `tests/scripts/scenarios/` that goes through the real commands: start, `in_review`, `atm task review request-changes`, then `atm loop next --claim` hands the task back to its agent; the same after approve.
- A `loop_rules` unit test with a `waiting` record from this worktree and one from another.

tasks.name: comments.md: a comment's body or path can't forge another comment, reply or heading
tasks.description:
Audit findings R1 and R2 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#r1-high-security-a-comment-body-can-forge-a-reply-from-anyone-checked)).

- **Body:** `crates/atm-review/src/files.rs:219-224` writes body lines verbatim, one level deeper than the comment, which is where a reply's `- **author** · at · cN` line goes. A body line of that shape is read back (`files.rs:436-446`) as a reply by whoever it names; the watch tells it to agents as a person's word.
- **Path:** `files.rs:186-204` writes `## {path}:{a}-{b} · round N · tK` with the path as given; nothing refuses a newline in it, so a path can add a heading or a resolved comment by the user.

## Change
- Escape, when writing, every body line that `read_item` or `read_heading` would accept (a marker the reader strips), or keep bodies in fenced blocks; existing files still read as before.
- Refuse a comment `path` with control characters, and one not among the round's files, in `rules::comment` (CLI and REST alike, `review_requests.rs:265-272`).
- Record the rule in `docs/security-architecture.md` (B2, I6's row or a new invariant).

## Tests
atm-review unit tests: a body containing a reply-shaped line and a heading-shaped line round-trips as one comment's body; a path with `\n` is refused; a path not in the round is refused.

tasks.name: Revisions from a review's round files are checked before git sees them (a Rev type for atm-vcs)
tasks.description:
Audit findings R3 and the `Rev` abstraction ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#r3-high-security-revisions-from-roundsnjson-reach-git-unchecked-checked-path-effect-suspected)).

`RoundKind`'s `base` and `head` are free strings from `rounds/N.json`, a committed and mergeable file. `crates/atm-review/src/rounds.rs:166-169` passes them to `tree_of` (`git rev-parse <head>^{tree}`) and `tree_after` (`git read-tree <base>`) in `crates/atm-vcs/src/diff.rs:297`, `:352`, without `commit_sha` (`diff.rs:119`) or `--end-of-options`. So do `file_in`, `diff_trees`, `gitlink_in`, `blob_in`, `message` and `in_history`. A value starting with `-` becomes an option to git, run just by opening the review page.

## Change
- Validate `base` and `head` as full hexadecimal object IDs when a round is read (`model.rs`); a round that fails is refused with a clear error.
- Introduce a `Rev` newtype in atm-vcs (a hex object ID, or a name checked not to start with `-` and with no NUL), and make every git-facing method take it, so an unchecked string can't reach git again.
- Add `--end-of-options` where git supports it.

## Tests
- atm-vcs unit tests: each method refuses a revision starting with `-`.
- A `tests/scripts/reviews/` test: a review whose `rounds/1.json` has `"base": "--index-output=x"` shows an error and writes no file.

tasks.name: Who is an agent: decided from positive evidence of a person, not a claude: prefix
tasks.description:
Audit finding L2 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#l2-high-security-the-review-gate-rests-on-the-actors-name-starting-with-claude-checked-in-part)). To be designed with Hakan: it changes who atm treats as a person.

`agent_identity` (`crates/atm-lib/src/actor.rs:28`) falls back to the git user name unless `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is set, and `is_agent` (`crates/atm-common/src/edits.rs:239`) is `starts_with("claude:")`. So an agent in Codex, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode or Gemini (all installed by `atm agents install`), or one passing `--agent '<a name>'`, counts as a person: `state.rs:272` lets it mark a `blocker` task done with no review, and a `batch` task gets no `sprint_review: pending`.

## Options to decide
- Detect the other harnesses' environment variables, and give them identities of their own.
- Inside a harness session, refuse an `--agent` or `ATM_AGENT` that would produce a person's identity.
- Treat an actor as a person only on positive evidence (the app or server path through `user_identity`, or an interactive terminal with no harness variables).

## Tests
Scenarios: each harness's environment gives an agent identity; `--agent 'Hakan'` inside a Claude Code session is refused or still an agent; a blocker task can't be done without review from any of them.

tasks.name: Release: the app compiles without the signing secrets; secrets in a release environment
tasks.description:
Audit findings A1 and A5 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#a1-medium-high-security-signing-secrets-are-in-the-environment-while-the-app-compiles-checked)). With Hakan: the GitHub settings (an environment, a tag ruleset) are his to apply.

- **A1:** `.github/workflows/release.yml:130-144` runs `tauri build` (every crate's build script and proc macro, the npm packages) with the updater key, its password and the notary key in its environment. Compile both targets in an earlier step without secrets (`cargo build --release --locked -p atm-app --target …`), then bundle and sign, where cargo has nothing left to build. Or bundle unsigned and sign the archive in its own step.
- **A5:** no job declares an `environment:` and the only ruleset covers `main`. Propose a `release` environment restricted to `v*` tags holding the signing and deploy-key secrets, a tag ruleset for `v*`, and a workflow check that the tag's commit is on `origin/main`.
- Pin the release, Homebrew and skills workflows' runners by version, as CI's are (A11).

## Tests
`dashboard/tests/unit/ci-workflow.test.ts`: no step that runs `cargo build` or `tauri build` has a signing secret in its `env`; the release jobs name the environment; runners are pinned.

tasks.name: Files named by --*-file options: inside the project or the temp folder, never a key file, at most 1 MiB
tasks.description:
Audit findings A2, C1 and C17's file part ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#c1-medium-security-every---file-option-reads-any-path-of-any-size-checked-see-a2)).

`cwd.join(file)` with an absolute path is that path, so `atm task edit X --description-file ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (a pre-approved command) puts a key in `tasks.json`, which `atm vcs commit` commits. No size cap either. Seven call sites: `task/add.rs:117`, `:189`, `task/edit.rs:99`, `review.rs:317`, `:752`, `:841`, `db.rs:191`; they also report a missing file three different ways.

## Change
One `read_option_file(cwd, option, file) -> Result<String>` and `read_option_json(...)` in `atm-cli`: canonicalize; allow only paths inside the project or the system temp folder; refuse dot-folders and key files (the same check as `atm-docs`' key-file rule); cap at 1 MiB; one wording and exit code (2) for a file that can't be used. Use it at every call site. Update `docs/security-architecture.md` (B1/B2: a new entry point rule).

## Tests
`tests/scripts/` cases: an absolute path outside the project, `~/.ssh/...`, a symlink out of the project, a 2 MiB file, `/dev/zero`: each refused with exit 2; a scratch file in the temp folder and one in the project accepted.

tasks.name: The review watch re-judges comments and decisions that weren't about my work yet
tasks.description:
Audit findings R5, R6 and R12 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#r5-high-bug-the-watch-marks-a-comment-seen-before-judging-it-reported-confirms-my-earlier-suspicion)).

- **R5:** `crates/atm-lib/src/review_listen.rs:433` puts every comment into `seen` (and the saved cursor) before judging it, so one judged not about the agent's work is never told, even after the agent's commit touches its file, or after the agent starts a task a person reviewed first. Decisions alike (`:464`). Only what was told, or skipped for its author, goes into `seen`; the rest is judged again each look while the review is open.
- **R6:** `seen` is keyed by `review/cN`, and a merge renumbers clashing IDs. Key it by ID with author and time (or a hash of them).
- **R12:** several watches of one agent share one lease file (the first to end deletes it) and overwrite each other's cursor. One lease per process, and merge the cursor under a lock.

## Tests
`tests/scripts/reviews/listening.test.mjs`: a comment on a file the agent touches only in a later commit is told after that commit; a comment made before the agent starts the task is told once it starts; two watches, one ending, leave the other's lease.

tasks.name: Errors: usage errors and conflicts are typed (Invalid, a new Conflict), so the server answers 400 and 409, not 500
tasks.description:
Audit findings C2, C17 and H3 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#c2-medium-bug-usage-errors-and-claimed-by-another-reach-the-dashboard-as-http-500-checked)).

`crates/atm-api/src/routes.rs:122` maps every `Error::Failed` to 500, but about 22 places build usage errors as `Failed { code: 2 }` and four build "claimed by another" as `Failed { code: 4 }`. The tasks route (`routes/tasks.rs:71-78`) maps errors its own way. Unknown task and unknown sprint are built as different variants in different modules.

## Change
- The `code: 2` cases become `Error::Invalid`; add `Error::Conflict(String)` (exit 4, HTTP 409) for claims.
- `routes/tasks.rs` uses `error_response`.
- One exit-code table (0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 nothing available, 4 conflict, and a separate code for a wait's timeout) in `atm-common`, mapped in one place; document it in `docs/agent/` (agents read exit codes).
- "No such task" is `NotFound` everywhere (one `task_at(work, id)` helper next to `Working`).

## Tests
atm-api route tests: a too-long note is 400, a claim held by another is 409, an unknown task is 404. CLI scenarios keep their exit codes.

tasks.name: Vocabulary IDs and sprint names are shell-safe; reserved sprint names refused
tasks.description:
Audit findings C3 and L13 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#c3-medium-security-status-type-and-priority-ids-and-sprint-names-arent-shell-safe-checked)).

`crates/atm-common/src/vocabulary.rs:211-215` accepts any non-empty status, type or priority ID, and sprint names only refuse outer spaces and length, while releases and components use `valid_short_id`. Agents paste these into commands (`atm task state … <status>`, `--sprint '<name>'`). And `backlog`, `new`, `active`, `next` are accepted as sprint names (`crates/atm-lib/src/sprints.rs:263`, and `rename_sprint`), after which `--to backlog` can never mean that sprint.

## Change
- `valid_short_id` on the IDs in `terms()`.
- Sprint names: letters, digits, space, `.`, `_`, `-`, `&` (the current sprint has one) and the like; no `$`, backtick, `;`, `|`, quotes, newlines. Decide the set from the existing names (`atm sprint list --all`) so nothing existing breaks.
- Refuse the four reserved words, case-insensitively, in `checked_name` and `rename_sprint`.
- Note it in `docs/security-architecture.md` I8.

## Tests
`tests/scripts/scenarios/security.json`: a status `done$(x)` and a sprint `s1;x` are refused on load and on add; `atm sprint add backlog` is refused.

tasks.name: ATM_NOW only in test builds; lease minutes and timeouts bounded
tasks.description:
Audit findings C4, C5, C16 and L9 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#c4-medium-security-atm_now-replaces-the-clock-in-release-builds-checked)).

- **C4:** `crates/atm-common/src/time.rs:8-13` lets `ATM_NOW` replace the clock in every build; claim liveness reads `now()`, so `ATM_NOW=2099-… atm loop next --claim` takes every other agent's task. Honour it only when a second, test-only variable is set too (the CLI suite sets both), or only in debug builds; check what `tests/scripts/` needs first.
- **L9:** `meta.lease_minutes` takes any positive number, `inf` too: clamp it (at most a year) and use `saturating_add` in `lease_until` and `offered_to`.
- **C5:** `--timeout 1e20` panics in `review.rs:623`: `Duration::try_from_secs_f64`.
- **C16:** `parse_iso` accepts seconds 60 and 61; the next task number `highest + 1` can wrap (`keys.rs:108`): refuse and `checked_add`.

## Tests
Scenarios: a lease from another agent stays live under `ATM_NOW` alone; `lease_minutes: 1e300` keeps claims alive; `--timeout 1e20` exits 2; `parse_iso("…T23:59:60Z")` is None.

tasks.name: One rule for a met dependency, live claims and a task's stage
tasks.description:
Audit findings L4, L7, L10 and L11 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#l4-medium-inconsistency-a-skipped-dependency-blocks-until-it-is-archived-then-counts-as-done-checked)).

- **L4:** a skipped dependency blocks while it is in `tasks.json` (`crates/atm-common/src/rules.rs:164`) and counts as met once archived (`:176`); `foreign.rs:321` has a third rule. Decide with the state machine (ATM-633) whether a skipped dependency is met, and write one `dependency_met(kind, resolution)` used for live, archived and foreign tasks; `archived` returns the archived task's kind, not a bool (a `Dependencies { tasks, archive }` type replaces the five "is it archived" closures).
- **L7:** `status.rs:117` and `summary.rs:622` hand stored claims to `next_task`; `next_task_for` drops expired ones first. One read-only `live_claims(store, now)` for all three.
- **L10:** `todo_command` (`changes.rs:397`) uses the default vocabulary and counts expired claims: use the project's vocabulary and live claims.
- **L11:** keep `query::task_stage`, delete `releases::stage_of`.

## Tests
Unit tests for each rule; a scenario where an agent's claim has expired and `project status` names the same next task as `loop next`.

tasks.name: Sprint and archive rules: pending sprint reviews aren't archived, claims seen in every worktree, unarchive deduplicates
tasks.description:
Audit findings L3, L6 and L8 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#l6-medium-bug-archiving-drops-batch-tasks-from-the-end-of-sprint-review-checked)).

- **L6:** `archivable_by` (`crates/atm-common/src/archive.rs:101`) moves done batch tasks with `sprint_review: pending`; `close_sprint` then never asks about them. Keep them out of the archive until reviewed.
- **L8:** sprint close, delete and move decide "claimed" from this copy's status only (`crates/atm-lib/src/sprints.rs:658`, `:805`, `:932`): also refuse a task with a live claim in the claims store (another worktree).
- **L3:** `atm db unarchive T-1 T-1` writes the task twice (`crates/atm-lib/src/archive.rs:345`): deduplicate the IDs keeping order; consider refusing duplicate IDs in `load_tasks` (or have `atm doctor` already catch it).

## Tests
Scenarios for each: a pending batch task stays after `atm db archive`; closing a sprint while a task is claimed in another worktree is refused; `unarchive` of a key and its alias adds one task.

tasks.name: atm db init --meta-file on an existing project changes only the keys it may
tasks.description:
Audit finding L5 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#l5-medium-bug-atm-db-init---meta-file-on-an-existing-project-overwrites-any-meta-key-checked)).

`crates/atm-lib/src/settings.rs:80-85` inserts every key of the file into an existing project's `meta`, checking only the vocabularies. A re-run (what `/atm-create-tasks` does) with `key` changes the project key without `key_history` (bypassing `set_project_key`); `format`, `next_number`, `next_id`, `key_history`, `sprints`, `releases` or `archived` are replaced too.

## Change
On an existing project accept an allow-list (project, description, statuses, types, priorities, default_priority, labels, components, review, workflow, archive settings, lease_minutes and the like); refuse the others with a message naming the command that changes each (`atm project key`, `atm sprint …`). Also: `vocab rename` rebuilds entries from `id`, `label`, `kind` and drops other keys (`settings.rs:450-477`): edit the stored entry in place.

## Tests
Scenarios: `key`, `format` and `sprints` in the file of an existing project are refused, nothing written; `description` is changed.

tasks.name: Review pages: reversed line ranges refused, git status renames parsed, a decision reaches all its tasks or none
tasks.description:
Audit findings R4, H1, R7 and R14 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#r4-medium-bug-a-reversed-line-range-panics-page-rendering-checked)).

- **R4:** `crates/atm-review/src/rounds.rs:382-384` panics on `lines: (5, 3)` (`mapped[0]` of an empty list). Require `1 <= first <= last` in `rules::comment` and `read_heading`, and guard `follow`.
- **H1:** `crates/atm-vcs/src/lib.rs:622-623` cuts 3 bytes off every `git status -z` record, also a rename's second field, which has no prefix: `README.md` becomes `DME.md`, and an old path starting with a multibyte character panics. Parse R/C entries as two fields; `entry.get(3..)`.
- **R14:** `diff.rs:166` lists changed files without `-z`, so paths with tabs or quotes come back C-quoted; type changes show as modified. Use `-z`.
- **R7:** `reviews.rs:653`, `:671` writes the review's decision, then changes each task; a failure on the second task leaves them split. Check every task's transition first (as `openings` does for create), then write.

## Tests
atm-review and atm-vcs unit tests for each; a `tests/scripts/reviews/` case with a staged rename of `éé/x.md` while a live review is open.

tasks.name: Document routes: .git refused in any case, logo through the files route's rules, GETs from other sites refused
tasks.description:
Audit findings H2, H5, H6, H7 and H8 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#h2-medium-security-the-git-refusal-is-case-sensitive-checked-exploitability-suspected)).

- **H2:** `crates/atm-docs/src/lib.rs:138-143` compares `.git` and `.agentic-task-manager` case-sensitively; on macOS `.GIT/config` may be served. Compare case-insensitively; on Windows also refuse segments ending in `.` or a space and `~` short names. First check with a test whether `git check-ignore` already refuses it.
- **H5:** GETs have no Origin check: any site can make the server write `recent.json` and run git (`at=:/<regex>`). Refuse a GET whose `Sec-Fetch-Site` is `cross-site` or whose `Origin` isn't the server's, except `/assets/`.
- **H6:** `at` may name a subtree: accept only a commit or a root tree a round recorded.
- **H7, H8:** the logo route (`crates/atm-db/src/jsongit/logo.rs:66`) follows symlinks and skips the files route's rules, and a logo that can't be read is a cached empty 200 (`routes/source.rs:284`): resolve and read it through `atm-docs`' image read, once, and answer 404 on failure.
- Update `docs/security-architecture.md` I11 and I12.

## Tests
`tests/scripts/serve.test.mjs`: `.GIT/config` refused; a cross-site GET refused and `recent.json` unchanged; a logo that is a symlink, or in `.git`, refused.

tasks.name: Server headers: every answer keeps nosniff and CORP, one policy for /assets/, documents at a revision cached by version
tasks.description:
Audit findings H9, H11, H12 and H13 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#reported-not-yet-checked-by-me-3)).

- **H11:** `crates/atm-api/src/lib.rs:195-200` falls back to a 200 without headers when the builder fails: fall back to a bare 500 with the security headers.
- **H12:** CompMD's bundle answers carry no `nosniff` or CORP and refuse HEAD, other assets send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` with CORP same-origin (`assets.rs:80`, `:108`): one policy for `/assets/`, stated in I11 and I13.
- **H9:** a document at a revision is cached a year as `immutable` across atm upgrades (`routes/documents.rs:34`): put atm's version in its tag.
- **H13:** stamp search with `generated_at`; `build.rs:109` must find exactly one CompMD version folder.

## Tests
`serve.test.mjs` "security headers": every `/assets/` answer, 404s included, has `nosniff`; a document's ETag changes with the version.

tasks.name: The service: never kill a pid it didn't start, a lock that can't be broken twice, owner-only state files
tasks.description:
Audit findings C6, C7, C10, C14 and C15 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#reported-not-yet-checked-by-me-2)).

- **C6:** `atm service stop` signals whatever pid a local port's whoami names (`crates/atm-cli/src/commands/maintenance.rs:464`, `:518`); another local user can answer on the port. Signal only a pid whose executable is atm and which owns the listening socket, or only report stray servers.
- **C14:** `wait_gone` sends SIGKILL by pid alone (`:404`): record the process's start time and signal only while it matches.
- **C7:** breaking a stale server lock (`:276`) races, so two runs can start two servers: rename the lock to a unique name atomically, then re-check, or use an OS file lock.
- **C10:** the state folder's 0700 is set only on creation (`crates/atm-common/src/home.rs:110`): set it on an existing or moved folder too, and create its files 0600.
- **C15:** `--open` runs `xdg-open` on Windows: use `explorer.exe <url>` (no shell; I24 lists the openers).

## Tests
`tests/scripts/serve.test.mjs`: a fake whoami on another port naming a pid isn't killed; two concurrent `atm service start` leave one server; an existing 0755 state folder becomes 0700.

tasks.name: The store: an unreadable claims store refuses writes; round and draft writes are crash- and race-safe
tasks.description:
Audit findings R9, R10, R11 and R13 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#reported-not-yet-checked-by-me-4)).

- **R9:** a claims store that fails to parse reads as empty (`crates/atm-db/src/jsongit/claims.rs:91`), and the next write drops every live claim: keep the error and refuse to write, as `load_tasks` does.
- **R10:** a round is written JSON first, diff second (`crates/atm-review/src/folder.rs:390`): write the diff first.
- **R11:** drafts are read-modify-write without a lock (`crates/atm-lib/src/review_drafts.rs:265`, `:299`, `:336`, `:372`): take `atm_fs::lock` on the drafts folder; after sending a draft, remove it before the next.
- **R13:** the merge driver takes ours on `meta` scalar conflicts without saying so (`crates/atm-db/src/jsongit/merge.rs:745`): report the conflict as task fields do.

## Tests
Unit tests: a corrupt claims store makes a change fail and leaves the file; a round folder with a JSON but no diff can't occur after a simulated failure between writes; two concurrent draft adds keep both; a `meta.workflow` conflict is reported.

tasks.name: Dashboard: loads guarded against stale answers; ReviewPage keyed by review
tasks.description:
Audit findings D1, D2 and the stale-guard abstraction ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#d1-medium-bug-project-loads-apply-stale-and-out-of-order-answers-checked)).

- **D1:** `dashboard/src/lib/state.svelte.ts:812-817` assigns the worktrees before checking the project is still shown; the guard compares the project ID only (two workspaces can have one); `refreshArchive` writes `this.archive` unchecked; `reload()` runs from the timer, focus, navigation and the app's events with no in-flight guard. Add a small `latest()` helper in `lib/` (a sequence token checked after every await) keyed on `workspace/project`, use it in `fetchAndApply`, `refreshArchive` and `refreshProjectSources`, skip a poll while one is in flight, and replace the other three guards with it (`ReviewsTab`, `AllProjectsBoard`, `DocumentViewer`).
- **D2:** `dashboard/src/lib/shell/ReviewsTab.svelte:255` reuses one `<ReviewPage>` across reviews, so a review-wide comment typed on CR-1 posts to CR-2 after following a link. Wrap it in `{#key page.review.id}`.

## Tests
Unit tests with a stubbed API that answers out of order (A's answer after B is shown changes nothing; an older poll after a newer one changes nothing); an e2e test in `reviews.spec.ts`: a draft review comment on one review isn't there after moving to another.

tasks.name: Dashboard links and storage: safeUrl for the submodule link, no . or .. in address segments, storage access never throws
tasks.description: Audit findings D3, D4, D5, D7 and D9 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#d3-medium-security-the-submodule-commit-link-skips-safeurl-checked)). - **D3:** `dashboard/src/lib/reviews/ReviewFile.svelte:119` puts `${moved.repository}/commit/${sha}` in an `href` without `safeUrl` (I14), and assumes GitHub's paths: `repoLinks(safeUrl(moved?.repository) ?? '')?.commit(sha)`. - **D4:** `safeTree` (`compmd.ts:446`) turns only raw `` into text; drop every `html` node CompMD would render as HTML (check CompMD 0.8.0's own policy first), and treat `area[href]` and SVG links like `a[href]` in `secureLinks`, `follow` and the app's external-link catcher. - **D5:** `app-tabs.svelte.ts:147` reads `sessionStorage` at module level, which throws when site data is blocked: wrap it in try/catch as `prefs.ts` does. - **D7:** `address.ts:124` accepts `.` and `..` as review or project IDs, which change the API path a write goes to: refuse them in `addressParams` and the URL builders. - **D9:** `decodeURIComponent` on a `#task=%E0` link throws (`compmd.ts:327`, `CompMd.svelte:261`): try/catch. ## Tests Unit tests: `url.test.ts`, `compmd.test.ts` (raw `` shows as text), `address.test.ts` (`..` refused), the tabs module loading with a throwing `sessionStorage`.

tasks.name: The app: windows.json written safely, deep links kept across a reload, a navigation guard, per-window badge
tasks.description:
Audit findings A3, A6, A7, A8, A9 and A10 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#a3-low-bug-windowsjson-writes-race-checked)).

- **A3:** `app/src-tauri/src/session.rs:283` shares one `windows.json.next` and holds no lock across write and rename: a write mutex, or a unique temporary name.
- **A8:** a deep link sent while a page reloads goes to the dead page's channel (`links.rs:84`): on `PageLoadEvent::Started` drop the window's links and menu channels, keeping `waiting`.
- **A6:** CompMD's frames count as local to Tauri, so the window's capability covers them; the guide says no capability lists them. Correct `docs/guides/tauri.md`, add a test that an invoke from a `compmd://` frame is refused, and consider refusing any invoke whose origin isn't the app page's. Add an `on_navigation` guard allowing only the app's own origin (A10's navigation part).
- **A9:** the Dock badge is app-wide but set from the calling window's workspace (`badge.rs:205`): keep per-window totals and show their sum, with `saturating_add`.
- **A7:** the menu is rebuilt on the main thread on every focus change, reading every project (`lib.rs:143`, `menu.rs:630`): read the IDs and names from the workspace's entries only.
- **A10 (updates):** check the downloaded app's version against the manifest's and the current one before installing (`updates.rs:46`).

## Tests
The app crate's unit tests for each (the session writes from two threads, the link kept after a page start, the badge sum).

tasks.name: Skills and packaging: atm version and atm docs pre-approved, the loop skill's sprint command, Homebrew inputs checked
tasks.description:
Audit findings A4, A11, A12 and A13 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#a4-low-bug-the-loop-skill-names-atm-sprints---json-checked-that-the-line-is-there)).

- **A4:** `skills/atm-loop-tasks/SKILL.md:174` names `atm sprints --json`; the command is `atm sprint list --json`.
- **A13:** every skill starts with `atm version` and points to `atm docs`, neither pre-approved in `skills/claude-code.json`: add both (read-only; check I2 and `skills.test.ts` allow them).
- **A12:** `packaging/homebrew-formula.sh` and `homebrew-cask.sh` put the version and checksums into Ruby unchecked: require `^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$` and `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`. The deploy-key pushes accept a new host key (`homebrew.yml:41`, `skills.yml:43`): pin GitHub's host keys. Both workflows check out the tag and refuse anything not a `v*` tag.
- **A11:** add Dependabot's `cargo` ecosystem, grouped like npm; pin the sandbox's images (`tests/sandbox/compose.yaml`, `Dockerfile`).

This changes skills: before the release PR merges, the security checklist (§3) applies.

## Tests
`dashboard/tests/unit/skills.test.ts` (the pre-approved list), `tests/scripts/packaging.test.mjs` (a bad version or checksum is refused), `ci-workflow.test.ts` (cargo in Dependabot, host keys pinned).

tasks.name: CLI output: bidi characters dropped, --json for every command, --agent not taken for a filter, claim hold refuses what it can't hold
tasks.description:
Audit findings C8, C9, C11, C12 and C13 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#reported-not-yet-checked-by-me-2)).

- **C9:** `output::clean` (`crates/atm-cli/src/output.rs:105`) keeps bidi and format characters (U+200B-200F, U+202A-202E, U+2060-2069, U+FEFF): drop them, sharing `py::printable`'s list (I30).
- **C11:** `service start/stop --json`, `db init --meta-file --json` and `vcs commit --record --json` print text or leave fields out: a JSON object each.
- **C13:** `task list --agent` is a filter, but `main.rs:396` takes any `--agent` as "run as someone else": rename the filter `--started-by` (keep `--agent` as a hidden alias for a release), or decide from the parsed command.
- **C12:** `claim hold` says it holds while its watcher quits when the shell's start time can't be read (`claim.rs:287`): refuse then.
- **C8:** each printed line with a UUID reopens the project and rereads the archive, twice in `say()`: one `Labeller` per process.

## Tests
`tests/scripts/output.test.mjs`: a task name with U+202E prints without it; each command's `--json` parses; `task list --agent x` still renews the caller's claim.

tasks.name: Dashboard rules from atm: kind, priority and stage from derived; status IDs never compared
tasks.description:
Audit findings D6, D12, D11 and D13 ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#reported-not-yet-checked-by-me-5)).

- **D6:** the dashboard calls `kindOf(` in about 45 places, `priorityOf` in 7 and `stageOf` in 4, though atm sends `derived.kind`, `derived.priority` and `derived.stage` (the guide: no domain logic in the UI). Add `kindOfTask(t)`, `priorityOfTask(t)`, `stageOfTask(t)` reading `derived`, falling back to the local rule only when it's missing, and use them.
- **D12:** `DepGraph.svelte:62` picks its focus by status IDs `in_progress` and `todo`: by kind.
- **D11:** Escape anywhere closes the details panel (`DetailPanel.svelte:194`): only when it's open and the event wasn't handled.
- **D13:** dragging the graph writes the whole view to localStorage on every pointer move: save on pointer up, or debounce `saveView`.

## Tests
Unit tests: a project with its own status IDs gets a graph focus; a task whose `derived.kind` differs from the local rule shows atm's; Escape in a composer doesn't close the panel.

tasks.name: Refactor atm-lib: Project::change returning a value, one task lookup, one expiry step, shared helpers
tasks.description:
Audit §2's repetition ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#repetition-and-abstractions-reported)). No behaviour changes; the existing tests are the check.

- `impl Project { fn change<T>(&mut self, f: impl FnMut(&mut Working) -> Result<T>) -> Result<T> }`, replacing about 30 `let mut outcome = None` sites.
- One `task_at(work, id) -> Result<usize>` (returning `NotFound`, saying when the task is archived) for the six copies.
- One `expire(work, vocab) -> Vec<Value>` for the four expiry preambles, and one `section(store, key)`.
- One `REWORK_STATES` (or `rules::awaits_agent`), one `id_of` (`Task::id()`), one `valid_label`, `find_release`, `in_open_pr`, `http_url`; `Vocabulary::active_sprint()` and `sprint_id_of(task)`; `set_or_remove(map, fields)`, `count_by_kind(vocab, tasks)`, `for_each_task_in_both(work, f)`.
- Status groups of reviews as methods on `atm_review::Status` (`is_decision`, `is_open`, `waits_on_reviewers`, `task_command`); one `actor_of`; `home::keyed_state_file(kind, parts)`.

Do it in steps, one helper per commit, with the full Rust suite between.

tasks.name: Refactor the front ends: one open-as-actor, one show for JSON or text, one dry-run rule; shared route and command shapes
tasks.description:
Audit §3-§5's repetition ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#8-cross-cutting-themes), theme 5). No behaviour changes but C17's dry-run rule.

## CLI
- A flattened `#[derive(Args)] struct As { agent: Option<String> }` with `fn open(&self, cwd) -> Result<Project>` (38 fields, 17 calls).
- `trait Shown { fn json(&self) -> Value; fn lines(&self) -> Vec<String>; }` and one `show(ctx, &out)` (92 branches).
- One `dry(ctx, what)` called after validating and resolving, never before (49 sites).

## Server
- A `Member { project, stamp }` held for a request, so a document GET opens the project once, not four times.
- `change::<Body, Out>(made, body, op)` for the eleven review change handlers; one `json_of`; one `conditional(request, tag, headers, load)`; `off_workers(f)`; `Served::is_own_host`.

## App
- One `with_user(state, w, p, |project| …)` for the fourteen review commands; `fn locked(m)`; `impl From<tauri::Error>` and `From<io::Error>` for `AppError`; one command list that generates the manifest and the capability.

One area per commit, the full suite between.

tasks.name: Refactor the dashboard: one request helper, shared card state, ReviewPage and state.svelte.ts split
tasks.description:
Audit §7's repetition ([the report](docs/codebase-audit-2026-11.md#repetition-and-abstractions-reported-4)). No behaviour change; the e2e suite is the check.

- One `request<T>(url, {method, body, since})` in `api/http.ts` returning `{status, body, etag}` and mapping `{error}` the same way, for the six fetch wrappers; URL building only in `http.ts`; `ipcFetch` honours `init` (D14).
- One `formatAgo` and `formatDateTime` in `format.ts` for the three "ago" formats and the bare `toLocaleString()` calls.
- `taskCardState(task)`, `<SprintBadge>`, `<TaskWaits>` for `TaskCard` and `KanbanCard`.
- Split `ReviewPage.svelte` (1,855 lines: the file tree, submit, overview, comments, keys) and `state.svelte.ts` (1,146: the saved view, the app update, the project cache, the loader).
- Start moving `app.css`'s component styles into their components (`.detail-*` first); inline `font-size:13px` and colours in `DetailPanel` become classes on tokens.
- Hand-made popovers (Progress, Activity), the project selector's listbox and the card's `div role=button` become Bits UI pieces or buttons.

One piece per commit.

tasks.name: A review's back arrow goes back to where it was opened from (task details, Kanban, the reviews lists, the Omniboard), with Back and Forward by address
tasks.description:
Reported by Hakan (2026-11-20): the back arrow on a review page always goes to the project's reviews list (`ReviewsTab.svelte:263-264`, `backHref={listAddress}`). A review can be opened from many places: a task's details, a Kanban card, a project's Reviews tab, the All projects reviews page, the Omniboard, a link in task text. Back should return there.

## Change
- Model each of those places as an address (most already are; the details panel over a page is `?task=`), so where a review was opened from is the previous address of the tab's history.
- The review page's back arrow goes back in the tab's history when its previous entry is in this app, labelled with where it goes ("← Task ATM-12", "← Kanban", "← All reviews"); only a review opened with no history (a new tab, a deep link) falls back to the project's reviews list.
- Back and Forward (the browser's, the app's keys and menu) then move through the same entries, consistently, as `docs/tabs-and-navigation-design.md` (ATM-653) describes; go through `lib/navigation.ts`, never `history` directly.

## Tests
E2e tests: a review opened from task details, from a Kanban card, from the All projects reviews page and from the Omniboard returns there on the back arrow, with the details panel open again where it was; Forward goes back to the review; a review opened in a new tab goes to its reviews list.

tasks.name: Live review: an update to the diff never flickers or moves either pane; the file or document being read stays where it is
tasks.description:
Reported by Hakan (2026-11-20): in a live review, the diff updates as the working copy changes (`ReviewsTab.svelte` asks again every 2 s in the browser, on a change in the app). Those updates must never flicker, and never move the scroll of the file tree (left) or the diffs (right). A document being read, or a file chosen on the left, stays where it is, as far as the update allows.

## Change
- Measure first: an e2e test on a live review that changes the working copy while a file is chosen and the pane is scrolled into it, sampling every frame (as ATM-656's test does): the pane's scroll, the chosen file's top, and whether any drawn block goes blank or is replaced.
- Then fix what the measurement shows: keep the files' components and their drawn code and documents across an update (keyed by path, the same text not drawn again), keep the scroll of both panes, and hold the file or line being read in place when files above it grow or shrink.

## Tests
That e2e test, for a change in another file, in the file being read (above and below the place read), and a file added above; in Chromium and WebKit (`@webkit`).

Reported by Hakan (2026-11-20): the title bar's line runs under the selected tab too, so only its colour says it is selected. The selected tab should have no line under it and join the page under it, as a browser's does.

tasks.name: A review's image files show their images (before and after), not only "binary"
tasks.description:
Reported by Hakan (2026-11-20, e.g. CR-60's screenshots): a binary file is rightly not copied into a review's round as a diff, but a file of a known type should still show when opened. Every image the viewer knows (png, jpeg, gif, webp, svg) shows its old and new image on the review's Diffs tab, instead of *A binary file: listed, not shown.*

## Change
- **atm-docs:** `read_image_at(vcs, revision, path)`: an image's bytes as a commit or tree has it, with `read_document_at`'s checks (the path's, a regular file, not ignored, the size limit) and `read_image`'s (only the image types, bytes matching their name); the two share one lookup.
- **atm-lib / atm-api:** `…/files?path=&at=<revision>`, as `…/documents?path=&at=` (kept by the browser when `at` is a full object ID); the app's `file_of` command takes `at` too (I27).
- **Dashboard:** a binary file of an image type shows its sides (removed: the old; added: the new; modified: both, side by side, labelled), each loaded from its revision; another binary file stays listed, not shown.
- **Docs:** `docs/security-architecture.md` I11 (the files route takes `at`, its checks) and `docs/multi-project-api.md`.

## Tests
atm-docs unit tests (an image at a revision; refused when it isn't one, or isn't an image); the route's tests on its fake; the app command's; an e2e test that a review's added and modified images show.

tasks.name: A review's source view draws no line between two lines
tasks.description:
Hakan: lines were drawn between each line of a review's source view.

## Cause
Each line's row (its tint and its number) is placed at the code's measured line height, a fraction of a pixel (20.8 px). Where two rows meet, both half cover the same pixel, so their tints blend into a line between every two lines.

## Change
`dashboard/src/lib/reviews/DiffCode.svelte`: `rowOf` puts each row's edges on whole pixels, so the rows tile.

## Tests
The Split Wrap test in `reviews.spec.ts` checks that every row is on whole pixels and starts where the one before it ends, wrapped and not.

tasks.name: WebKit: a jump to a file still moves for a few frames, about 1 run in 8 (19 px; once 5,803 px)
tasks.description:
The e2e test *a jump to a file stays on it while the files above it are drawn* (`reviews.spec.ts`, ATM-656) fails in WebKit about 3 runs in 24, at the commit before ATM-690's changes too, so it is not new with them.

## What it shows
The file jumped to arrives, then sits 18 to 19 px off (one line's height) for 2 to 8 frames before it comes back:

```
f047.rs: [1,-18,-18,-18,-18,-18,-18,1,1,…]
```

Once it was 5,803 px off for a frame:

```
f093.rs: [1,-5803,1,1,…]
```

## To do
Find which file above it grows by a line after the jump (and what makes it 5,803 px once), and why the place read isn't kept for those frames, as ATM-656 and ATM-687 meant. Measure in WebKit with `--repeat-each=24`; never only rerun it.
